    private val ATTEMPT_GRID = 60

    // ------------------------------------------------------------- text basics

    fun isUnsafeRewardText(text: String): Boolean {
        val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(text)
        if (value.isEmpty()) return false
        return UNSAFE_REWARD_TEXT.any { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it).let { term -> term.isNotEmpty() && term in value } }
    }

    /**
     * Whether (x, y) is an X already tapped in this ad. OCR boxes and corner
     * matches move 1-3 px between frames, so an exact match tapped the same
     * dead X again (review 2026-11-12 #7).
     */
    fun alreadyTried(tried: Collection<Pair<Int, Int>>, x: Int, y: Int, tolerancePx: Int = TRIED_TOLERANCE_PX): Boolean =
        tried.any { (tx, ty) -> kotlin.math.abs(tx - x) <= tolerancePx && kotlin.math.abs(ty - y) <= tolerancePx }

    private const val TRIED_TOLERANCE_PX = 16

    /** The status bar's shade: the user is in it, so the collector waits. */
    fun isUserShade(packageName: String?): Boolean = packageName?.trim() == "com.android.systemui"

    fun isSystemPackage(packageName: String?): Boolean {
        val value = packageName?.trim().orEmpty()
        return value.isEmpty() || value in SYSTEM_PACKAGES
    }

    /** The app's bottom tab bar must be visible: only the bottom 18% counts. */
    /** On one of the app's own pages that has no tab bar (AHEALTH 甇亥?). */
    fun onSubPage(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Boolean =
        profile.altChromeTerms.isNotEmpty() && hasAppChrome(snapshot, profile) &&
            !hasAppChrome(snapshot, profile.copy(altChromeTerms = emptyList()))

    fun hasAppChrome(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Boolean {
        if (profile.chromeTerms.isEmpty()) return true
        if (profile.altChromeTerms.isNotEmpty()) {
            val all = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(snapshot.text)
            if (profile.altChromeTerms.any { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it).let { t -> t.isNotEmpty() && t in all } }) return true
        }
        val bandTop = (snapshot.height * CHROME_BAND).toInt()
        val bandText = snapshot.boxes
            .filter { it.bounds.top >= bandTop }
            .map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it.text) }
        val terms = profile.chromeTerms.map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        val hits = terms.count { term -> bandText.any { term in it } }
        return hits >= minOf(CHROME_MIN_TERMS, terms.size)
    }

    private const val CHROME_BAND = 0.82
    private const val CHROME_MIN_TERMS = 2

    // ----------------------------------------------------------- reward picking

    /**
     * Reward candidates in tap order. Mirrors `Snapshot.candidates` +
     * `_pick_reward`: node boxes win when any exist, then the terms' own
     * priority decides, not the match score.
     */
    fun rewardCandidates(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): List<TextBoxMatch> {
        val nodeMatches = snapshot.copy(boxes = snapshot.boxesFrom(TextSource.NODE))
            .matches(profile.rewardTerms, profile.avoidTerms, profile.exactTerms)
        val ocrMatches = snapshot.copy(boxes = snapshot.boxesFrom(TextSource.OCR))
            .matches(profile.rewardTerms, profile.avoidTerms, profile.exactTerms)
        val chosen = when {
            !profile.useNodes -> ocrMatches
            nodeMatches.isNotEmpty() -> nodeMatches
            else -> ocrMatches
        }
        return chosen.sortedBy { termPriority(it.text, profile) }
    }

    fun termPriority(text: String, profile: AppProfile): Int {
        val label = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(text)
        val exact = profile.exactTerms.map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) }.toSet()
        profile.rewardTerms.forEachIndexed { index, term ->
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(term)
            if (value.isEmpty()) return@forEachIndexed
            val matches = if (value in exact) label == value else value in label
            if (matches) return index
        }
        return profile.rewardTerms.size
    }

    /** Stable key for the per-button repeat limit; OCR jitter must not escape it. */
    /** A button's identity by its words alone (positions move a pixel or two). */
    fun dropKey(text: String): String = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(text)

    /**
     * The same button by where it sits, for when OCR reads its words a little
     * differently each time (蝳桃??/ ???/ 瞉抒?? 2026-11-16).
     */
    fun dropSpot(target: Target): String =
        "${Math.floorDiv(target.centerX, DROP_SPOT_GRID)},${Math.floorDiv(target.centerY, DROP_SPOT_GRID)}"

    const val DROP_SPOT_GRID = 120

    /** A non-ad button that left the app this many times in a row is not tapped again. */
    const val LEAD_OUTS_TO_DROP = 2

    fun attemptKey(target: Target): String {
        val prefix = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(target.text).take(6)
        return "$prefix@${Math.floorDiv(target.centerX, ATTEMPT_GRID)},${Math.floorDiv(target.centerY, ATTEMPT_GRID)}"
    }

    fun pickReward(
        snapshot: Snapshot,
        profile: AppProfile,
        attempts: Map<String, Int>,
        allowed: ((Target, Snapshot) -> Boolean)? = null
    ): Target? = eligibleRewards(snapshot, profile, attempts, allowed).firstOrNull()

    /**
     * Every button on this screen the collector would tap, in tap order
     * ([pickReward] takes the first). The scan (2026-11-15) counts them.
     */
    fun eligibleRewards(
        snapshot: Snapshot,
        profile: AppProfile,
        attempts: Map<String, Int> = emptyMap(),
        allowed: ((Target, Snapshot) -> Boolean)? = null
    ): Sequence<Target> = sequence {
        val pageText = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(snapshot.text)
        val seen = HashSet<Pair<Int, Int>>()
        for (candidate in rewardCandidates(snapshot, profile)) {
            val label = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(candidate.text)
            if (label.isEmpty()) continue
            if (isUnsafeRewardText(candidate.text)) continue
            if (profile.statusTerms.any { term ->
                    val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(term)
                    value.isNotEmpty() && value in label
                }
            ) continue
            val unavailable = profile.unavailablePairs.any { (term, marker) ->
                val t = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(term)
                val m = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(marker)
                t.isNotEmpty() && m.isNotEmpty() && t in label && m in pageText
            }
            if (unavailable) continue
            val center = candidate.centerX to candidate.centerY
            if (!seen.add(center)) continue
            val target = Target(candidate.text, candidate.bounds, candidate.score, candidate.source.name.lowercase())
            if (allowed != null && !allowed(target, snapshot)) continue
            if ((attempts[attemptKey(target)] ?: 0) >= profile.maxRepeatPerTarget) continue
            if (candidate.bounds.top < (snapshot.height * 0.035).toInt()) continue
            if (candidate.bounds.bottom > snapshot.height * 0.99) continue
            if (!validTapBounds(candidate.bounds, snapshot.width, snapshot.height)) continue
            // A greyed-out button (the node says not enabled) is not a reward yet.
            if (snapshot.disabled.any { it.containsPoint(candidate.centerX, candidate.centerY) }) continue
            yield(target)
        }
    }

    /**
     * How many rewards a scan saw on one tab, from the buttons of each page
     * it scrolled through. Pages overlap, so the same button may be seen
     * twice: each label counts as often as it appears on its fullest page
     * (a lower bound, never a double count).
     */
    fun scanCount(pages: List<List<Target>>): Int {
        val most = HashMap<String, Int>()
        for (page in pages) {
            page.groupingBy { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it.text) }.eachCount().forEach { (label, n) ->
                if (n > (most[label] ?: 0)) most[label] = n
            }
        }
        return most.values.sum()
    }

    /**
     * Draws a lottery sheet still offers. The red badges are tickets, not
     * draws (2026-11-16: 24 + 240 was reported as 265 draws): BIG costs 50
     * tickets, a normal draw 5, plus a free draw that is not cooling down.
     */
    fun lotteryAvailable(sheet: LineWalkRules.LotterySheet): Int =
        (sheet.counts["big"] ?: 0) / LOTTERY_BIG_TICKETS +
            (sheet.counts["normal"] ?: 0) / LOTTERY_NORMAL_TICKETS +
            if (sheet.free != null && sheet.cooldowns["free"].isNullOrEmpty()) 1 else 0

    const val LOTTERY_BIG_TICKETS = 50
    const val LOTTERY_NORMAL_TICKETS = 5

    /**
     * A direct claim (no ad, no dialog) that worked: the app is still on its
     * own screen and the tapped button is gone (?? -> 撌脤???/ 隞暺撌脤?摰?.
     * AHEALTH's "?? 10 暺" on 2026-11-12 ended as "changed" and was never
     * counted although the points were taken. LINE is excluded: it only counts
     * a reward from its dialog or the coin counter.
     */
    fun isDirectClaim(candidate: Target, after: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile, expectAd: Boolean): Boolean =
        !expectAd && !profile.lineRules && hasAppChrome(after, profile) &&
            refusalText(after) == null &&
            !stillOffered(candidate, after, profile)

    /**
     * The app turning the tap down: already done today, nothing new. Such a
     * notice hides the button, which used to count as a direct claim
     * (HAHAGO 2026-11-14: "隞撌脖??喲??詨??郊?賂?").
     */
    fun refusalText(snapshot: Snapshot): String? {
        val text = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(snapshot.text)
        return REFUSAL_TERMS.firstOrNull { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) in text }
    }

    val REFUSAL_TERMS = listOf(
        "撌脖??喲?", "撌脖?隡?", "隞撌脩偷??, "隞予撌脩偷??, "撌脩?蝪賢", "?典歇蝪賢",
        "撌脩?????, "撌脤???", "隞撌脤???, "?予??", "???",
        "already claimed", "come back tomorrow"
    )
    val REFUSAL_CLOSE_TERMS = listOf("蝣箄?", "蝣箏?", "?仿?鈭?, "??", "憟賜?", "OK")

    /**
     * InMobi's end card whose only control is "罈 Skip to Google Play" (it
     * opens the store; never tapped). Seen on BITWALK 2026-11-13 16:11 and
     * 2026-11-14 10:42: waiting cannot end it.
     */
    fun isPlayStoreEndCard(snapshot: Snapshot): Boolean =
        TextMatch.normalizeLoose("skip to goog").let { it in TextMatch.normalizeLoose(snapshot.text) }

    fun stillOffered(candidate: Target, after: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Boolean {
        val key = attemptKey(candidate)
        return rewardCandidates(after, profile).any {
            attemptKey(Target(it.text, it.bounds, it.score, it.source.name.lowercase())) == key
        }
    }

    fun validTapBounds(
        bounds: Box,
        screenWidth: Int,
        screenHeight: Int,
        maxAreaRatio: Double = 0.35
    ): Boolean =
        bounds.width > 0 && bounds.height > 0 &&
            bounds.left >= 0 && bounds.top >= 0 &&
            bounds.right <= screenWidth && bounds.bottom <= screenHeight &&
            bounds.area <= (screenWidth.toLong() * screenHeight * maxAreaRatio).toLong()

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ dialogs

    /** The central text line that proves a dialog ("?剖?", "?函敺?"). */
    fun dialogAnchor(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): TextBox? {
        val extra = profile.dialogTermsExtra
        val terms = if (hasAppChrome(snapshot, profile)) {
            DIALOG_STRONG_TERMS + extra
        } else {
            DIALOG_TERMS + extra
        }
        val wanted = terms.map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        for (box in snapshot.boxes) {
            val cx = (box.bounds.left + box.bounds.right) / 2
            val cy = (box.bounds.top + box.bounds.bottom) / 2
            if (cx < snapshot.width * 0.1 || cx > snapshot.width * 0.9) continue
            if (cy < snapshot.height * 0.15 || cy > snapshot.height * 0.8) continue
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text)
            if (wanted.any { it in value }) return box
        }
        return null
    }

    fun isDialog(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Boolean =
        dialogAnchor(snapshot, profile) != null

    /** The short confirm button below the dialog text. */
    fun findDialogConfirm(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Target? {
        val anchor = dialogAnchor(snapshot, profile) ?: return null
        val confirm = CONFIRM_TERMS.map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) }.toSet()
        val adBlock = dialogAdBlock(snapshot, anchor)
        val hasOcr = snapshot.ocrCount() > 0
        var best: Target? = null
        for (box in snapshot.boxes) {
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text)
            if (value.isEmpty() || value.length > 8) continue
            // LINE's reward dialog embeds an ad between its text and ??.
            // A "蝣箄?" node inside that ad (invisible on screen) was tapped on
            // 2026-11-12 20:12 and opened Google Play. Nothing inside the ad
            // block is a dialog button.
            if (adBlock != null && adBlock.containsPoint(box.bounds.centerX, box.bounds.centerY)) continue
            // A button the screenshot cannot see is not a button the user
            // could press; when OCR ran, the text must be on screen.
            if (hasOcr && box.source == TextSource.NODE && !visibleOnScreen(snapshot, box, value)) continue
            if ("??" in value || "cancel" in value) continue
            if (isUnsafeRewardText(box.text)) continue
            if (!confirm.any { value == it || value.startsWith(it) }) continue
            val cx = (box.bounds.left + box.bounds.right) / 2
            val cy = (box.bounds.top + box.bounds.bottom) / 2
            if (cx < snapshot.width * 0.1 || cx > snapshot.width * 0.9) continue
            if (cy < anchor.bounds.top || cy > anchor.bounds.bottom + snapshot.height * 0.45) continue
            if (!validTapBounds(box.bounds, snapshot.width, snapshot.height, 0.1)) continue
            val target = Target(box.text, box.bounds, 100, "dialog_confirm")
            if (best == null || target.centerY < best.centerY) best = target
        }
        return best
    }

    /**
     * The ad embedded in a dialog: from its "AD" label down to the dialog's
     * own ??/蝣箄? below it (or 35% of the screen when none is found).
     */
    fun dialogAdBlock(snapshot: Snapshot, anchor: TextBox): Box? {
        val label = snapshot.boxes.firstOrNull { box ->
            TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text) == "ad" && box.bounds.top >= anchor.bounds.top
        } ?: return null
        val closeTerms = setOf("??", "close")
        val closeBelow = snapshot.boxes
            .filter { box ->
                TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text) in closeTerms &&
                    box.bounds.top > label.bounds.bottom
            }
            .minByOrNull { it.bounds.top }
        val bottom = closeBelow?.bounds?.top ?: (label.bounds.bottom + (snapshot.height * 0.35).toInt())
        return Box(0, label.bounds.top, snapshot.width, bottom)
    }

    private fun visibleOnScreen(snapshot: Snapshot, node: TextBox, value: String): Boolean {
        val cx = node.bounds.centerX
        val cy = node.bounds.centerY
        return snapshot.boxes.any { box ->
            box.source == TextSource.OCR &&
                TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text).contains(value) &&
                kotlin.math.abs(box.bounds.centerX - cx) < VISIBLE_MATCH_PX &&
                kotlin.math.abs(box.bounds.centerY - cy) < VISIBLE_MATCH_PX
        }
    }

    private const val VISIBLE_MATCH_PX = 120

    /**
     * The close button of the app's own help dialog ("隞暻潭??隞交?蚪TC嚗?).
     * It means no ad is available right now; it is never a reward.
     */
    fun findInfoDialogClose(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Target? {
        if (profile.infoDialogTerms.isEmpty()) return null
        val wanted = profile.infoDialogTerms.map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        val anchor = snapshot.boxes.firstOrNull { box ->
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text)
            wanted.any { it.isNotEmpty() && it in value }
        } ?: return null
        val closers = INFO_CLOSE_TERMS.map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) }.toSet()
        for (box in snapshot.boxes) {
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text)
            if (value !in closers) continue
            val cx = (box.bounds.left + box.bounds.right) / 2
            val cy = (box.bounds.top + box.bounds.bottom) / 2
            if (cx < snapshot.width * 0.2 || cx > snapshot.width * 0.8) continue
            if (cy <= anchor.bounds.top || cy > anchor.bounds.bottom + snapshot.height * 0.6) continue
            return Target(box.text, box.bounds, 100, "info_dialog_close")
        }
        return null
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ ad handling

    /**
     * Positive evidence that an ad is on screen. Close words alone are not
     * enough (the app's own pages have dismiss icons), which is why every branch
     * below names the evidence.
     */
    fun adEvidence(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Pair<Boolean, String> {
        if (AdActivityClassifier.classify(snapshot.foregroundActivity, profile.packageName) ==
            AdActivityClassifier.Kind.AD &&
            // The activity name can be stale: closing an ad back to the app does
            // not always raise a new window event. A full-screen ad never shows
            // the app's own bottom bar, so the bar on screen means the ad is gone
            // (LINE 2026-11-17 10:16: Back after the X left LINE altogether).
            !(profile.chromeTerms.isNotEmpty() && hasAppChrome(snapshot, profile))
        ) {
            return true to "ad_activity"
        }
        val pkg = snapshot.foregroundPackage?.trim().orEmpty()
        if (pkg.isNotEmpty() && pkg != profile.packageName && !isSystemPackage(pkg)) {
            return true to "external_package"
        }

        val loose = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(snapshot.text)
        if ((AD_HARD_MARKERS + profile.adHardMarkersExtra).any {
                val marker = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it)
                marker.isNotEmpty() && marker in loose
            }
        ) {
            return true to "hard_ad_marker"
        }
        if (hasAppChrome(snapshot, profile)) return false to "app_chrome"

        // 2026-11-13 19:58: WALK EARN's Lucky box / Claim opened an in-app
        // interstitial whose first frames are only a Google Play card with
        // "摰?" over a video - no countdown or X yet. Read as a risky web
        // page, Back cut the ad off and no reward came, so the same button was
        // tapped again and again. Inside the reward app with its tab bar gone,
        // a store card is an ad; the ad loop never taps "摰?".
        if (!profile.lineRules && (pkg.isEmpty() || pkg == profile.packageName) && hasStoreCard(loose)) {
            return true to "store_card_ad"
        }

        val countdown = hasAdCountdown(snapshot)
        val closeGlyph = hasCloseGlyph(snapshot)
        val raw = snapshot.text
        val hasAdWord = Regex("\\bAD\\b", RegexOption.IGNORE_CASE).containsMatchIn(raw)
        val hasMarker = AD_MARKERS.any {
            val marker = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it)
            marker.isNotEmpty() && marker in loose
        }
        if ((hasAdWord || hasMarker) && (countdown || closeGlyph)) {
            return true to "ad_marker_with_geometry"
        }
        if (countdown && closeGlyph) return true to "ad_timer_with_close"
        return false to "insufficient_evidence"
    }

    private val STORE_NAMES = listOf("google play", "googleplay", "app store")
    private val INSTALL_WORDS = listOf("摰?", "摰?", "install", "銝?", "download")

    /** An ad's store card: a store name and an install button together. */
    internal fun hasStoreCard(looseText: String): Boolean =
        STORE_NAMES.any { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) in looseText } &&
            INSTALL_WORDS.any { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) in looseText }

    /**
     * A box that is only an ad label ("Ad", "AD", "撱??", "Sponsored"). Used
     * at app start, where an app-open ad shows that label and a drawn X but
     * no countdown yet (WALK EARN, 2026-11-13 23:56).
     */
    fun hasAdBadge(snapshot: Snapshot): Boolean = snapshot.boxes.any {
        TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it.text) in AD_BADGES
    }

    private val AD_BADGES = setOf("ad", "撱??", "撟踹?", "sponsored", "ads")

    /**
     * Unity's "?閏 ????" at the top of an ad that offers no X. The user
     * found it is the way on (2026-11-14 22:38, BITWALK held seven minutes):
     * it opens the store, Back returns to the ad, and the ad goes on.
     * Only this short label near the top counts; "Install" and "Skip to
     * Google Play" are still never tapped.
     */
    fun findOpenStoreSkip(snapshot: Snapshot): TextBox? = snapshot.boxes.firstOrNull { box ->
        val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text).filter { it.isLetterOrDigit() }
        value == "????" && box.bounds.centerY < snapshot.height * 0.12 &&
            validTapBounds(box.bounds, snapshot.width, snapshot.height, 0.05)
    }

    /** "2p 撌脤???": the reward sheet that proves points were credited. */
    fun isRewardReceivedSheet(snapshot: Snapshot): Boolean =
        snapshot.boxes.any { Regex("\\d+\\s*[pP]\\s*撌脤???).containsMatchIn(it.text) }

    /**
     * "蝣箏?閬?甇Ｚ??摨瑞敶梢?? ??/ ??: the app asking whether to leave a
     * page. Yes is what Back meant (the run held here on 2026-11-14 21:01).
     */
    fun findLeaveConfirm(snapshot: Snapshot): Target? {
        val text = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(snapshot.text)
        if (LEAVE_PROMPTS.none { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) in text }) return null
        val yes = snapshot.boxes.firstOrNull { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it.text) in setOf("??, "蝣箏??ａ?", "?ａ?") }
            ?: return null
        return Target(yes.text, yes.bounds, 100, "leave_confirm")
    }

    private val LEAVE_PROMPTS = listOf("蝣箏?閬?甇Ｚ???, "蝣箏?閬??, "蝣箏??ａ?")

    /** The app's own "done" button on its reward sheet, exact label only. */
    fun findDone(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): TextBox? {
        if (profile.doneTerms.isEmpty()) return null
        val terms = profile.doneTerms.map { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it) }.toSet()
        return snapshot.boxes.firstOrNull { box ->
            TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text) in terms &&
                validTapBounds(box.bounds, snapshot.width, snapshot.height, 0.2)
        }
    }

    fun looksLikeAd(snapshot: Snapshot, profile: AppProfile): Boolean =
        adEvidence(snapshot, profile).first

    /** "蝚?3 ?誨????5 ?? -> (3, 5); either part may be unreadable. */
    fun adSequence(snapshot: Snapshot): Pair<Int?, Int?> {
        val pattern = Regex("(?:蝚?\\d+))??誨?(\\d+)??)
        for (box in snapshot.boxes) {
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text)
            val match = pattern.find(value) ?: continue
            return match.groupValues[1].toIntOrNull() to match.groupValues[2].toIntOrNull()
        }
        return null to null
    }

    fun hasAdCountdown(snapshot: Snapshot): Boolean {
        val pattern = Regex("\\d{1,2}(?:s|sec|蝘??")
        for (box in snapshot.boxes) {
            if (!pattern.matches(TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text))) continue
            if (box.bounds.left >= snapshot.width * 0.6 && box.bounds.top <= snapshot.height * 0.35) {
                return true
            }
        }
        return false
    }

    fun hasCloseGlyph(snapshot: Snapshot): Boolean =
        snapshot.boxes.any { TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it.text) in CLOSE_GLYPHS }

    fun isNextAdLabel(text: String, contentDescription: String = ""): Boolean {
        // Symbols such as ">>" lose their meaning under the loose normalisation
        // (punctuation is dropped), so the exact list uses the compact form.
        val compact = listOf(TextMatch.normalize(text), TextMatch.normalize(contentDescription))
        if (compact.any { it in NEXT_EXACT }) return true
        if (isUnsafeRewardText(text) || isUnsafeRewardText(contentDescription)) return false
        val normalized = listOf(TextMatch.normalizeLoose(text), TextMatch.normalizeLoose(contentDescription))
        return normalized.any { value ->
            value.isNotEmpty() && value.length <= NEXT_MAX_LABEL_LEN &&
                NEXT_SUBSTRINGS.any { it in value }
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ close / next

    /**
     * Close controls from text plus the corner templates.
     *
     * The text side uses the guard's own detector, so the collector inherits the
     * store-CTA rejection and the edge/centre rules the guard already proved.
     */
    fun findCloseTargets(
        snapshot: Snapshot,
        profile: AppProfile,
        cornerHits: List<GlyphHit>
    ): List<Target> {
        val targets = ArrayList<Target>()
        for (box in snapshot.boxes) {
            val node = NodeSnapshot(
                text = box.text,
                contentDescription = null,
                viewIdResourceName = null,
                className = null,
                clickable = false,
                left = box.bounds.left,
                top = box.bounds.top,
                right = box.bounds.right,
                bottom = box.bounds.bottom
            )
            val score = CloseButtonDetector.score(node, snapshot.width, snapshot.height)
            if (!score.matched) continue
            targets.add(Target(box.text, box.bounds, score.score, "close_text:${score.method}"))
        }
        for (hit in cornerHits) {
            if (hit.kind != "close") continue
            targets.add(Target("[X]", hit.bounds, 100 + (hit.score * 10).toInt(), "corner_close"))
        }
        // With the app's own bar visible, image matches low in the band are
        // usually app artwork (BITWALK's banner), so only the top 15% is trusted.
        val filtered = if (hasAppChrome(snapshot, profile)) {
            targets.filter {
                it.source != "corner_close" || it.centerY <= snapshot.height * 0.15
            }
        } else {
            targets
        }
        return dedupeByScore(filtered)
    }

    fun findNextTargets(
        snapshot: Snapshot,
        profile: AppProfile,
        cornerHits: List<GlyphHit>
    ): List<Target> {
        val targets = ArrayList<Target>()
        for (box in snapshot.boxes) {
            if (!isNextAdLabel(box.text)) continue
            targets.add(Target(box.text, box.bounds, 100, "next_text"))
        }
        if (!hasAppChrome(snapshot, profile)) {
            for (hit in cornerHits) {
                if (hit.kind != "next") continue
                // An icon-only >> is trusted only top-right; a chevron in ad
                // artwork opened Chrome on 2026-11-11.
                if (hit.bounds.centerX < snapshot.width * 0.75 || hit.bounds.centerY > snapshot.height * 0.2) continue
                targets.add(Target("[>>]", hit.bounds, (hit.score * 100).toInt(), "corner_next"))
            }
        }
        return dedupeByScore(targets)
    }

    private fun dedupeByScore(targets: List<Target>): List<Target> {
        val result = ArrayList<Target>()
        for (target in targets.sortedByDescending { it.score }) {
            val duplicate = result.any {
                kotlin.math.abs(it.centerX - target.centerX) < 40 &&
                    kotlin.math.abs(it.centerY - target.centerY) < 40
            }
            if (!duplicate) result.add(target)
        }
        return result
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import android.content.Context
import androidx.core.content.FileProvider
import java.io.File
import java.util.zip.ZipEntry
import java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream

/**
 * Zips the newest `collector_runs/run_*` directory into the existing
 * FileProvider export area, so a run record can leave the phone through the
 * normal share sheet instead of `adb run-as`.
 *
 * Run records live in the private files directory (screenshots included), so
 * only the finished zip is placed in `cache/exports`, which `file_paths.xml`
 * already exposes. The zip keeps the run directory name as its top folder, so
 * the private test-log repository can unpack it as one run.
 */
object CollectorRunExporter {

    data class ExportResult(val file: File, val uri: android.net.Uri)

    fun exportLatest(context: Context): ExportResult? =
        export(context, latestRunDir(context))

    fun latestRunDir(context: Context): File? =
        File(context.filesDir, "collector_runs")
            .listFiles { file -> file.isDirectory && file.name.startsWith("run_") }
            ?.maxByOrNull { it.name }

    fun export(context: Context, runDir: File?): ExportResult? {
        if (runDir == null || !runDir.isDirectory) return null
        val exportDir = File(context.cacheDir, "exports").apply { mkdirs() }
        val file = File(exportDir, "${runDir.name}.zip")
        runCatching {
            ZipOutputStream(file.outputStream().buffered()).use { zip ->
                runDir.walkTopDown().filter { it.isFile }.forEach { source ->
                    val relative = source.relativeTo(runDir).invariantSeparatorsPath
                    zip.putNextEntry(ZipEntry("${runDir.name}/$relative"))
                    source.inputStream().buffered().use { it.copyTo(zip) }
                    zip.closeEntry()
                }
            }
        }.onFailure {
            runCatching { file.delete() }
            return null
        }
        val uri = FileProvider.getUriForFile(
            context,
            "${context.packageName}.fileprovider",
            file
        )
        return ExportResult(file, uri)
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

/**
 * Decides whether a sequential "?券" run may launch its next app.
 *
 * The controller runs profiles one after another, so a user pressing 蝯? while
 * the first app is active used to be forgotten: the engine stopped, then the
 * next profile called `environment.start()` and the phone opened another app.
 * The same must not happen when the engine stopped itself because the phone was
 * locked, paused too long, or hit the run timeout.
 *
 * Pure so the rule can be tested without a phone.
 */
object CollectorRunPolicy {

    /** Engine end reasons after which no further app may be started. */
    private val STOPPING_REASONS = setOf(
        "stopped",
        "paused_too_long",
        "run_timeout",
        "cancelled",
        "error",
        // LINE's lottery is out of 5-ticket draws: the caller leaves for the
        // desktop and stops the guard, so the next app must not launch (2026-11-21).
        "lottery_tickets_low"
    )

    /**
     * Runs [items] in order and returns each one's end reason.
     *
     * Shared by the ?芸??嗅? tab and the adb `collector_run` entry, which used
     * to have their own loops - and the adb one still opened the next app after
     * `collector_stop`. [stopRequested] and [keyguardLocked] are read before
     * every item, so a stop pressed during item 1 means items 2 and 3 never
     * start.
     */
    suspend fun <T> runSequence(
        items: List<T>,
        stopRequested: () -> Boolean,
        keyguardLocked: () -> Boolean,
        runOne: suspend (T) -> String
    ): List<String> {
        val reasons = ArrayList<String>(items.size)
        var previous: String? = null
        for (item in items) {
            if (!shouldStartNext(stopRequested(), previous, keyguardLocked())) break
            previous = runOne(item)
            reasons.add(previous)
        }
        return reasons
    }

    /**
     * The 60-minute run cap applies only to a run with a number. 銝??賊? means
     * "until I press 蝯?" (review P1-4): BitWalk allows 50 ads a day and the
     * lottery can take hundreds of draws, both past an hour.
     */
    fun runCapApplies(rewardLimit: Int): Boolean = rewardLimit != CollectorLimits.UNLIMITED

    /**
     * Whether a pause may end the run after the pause limit. A pause the user
     * asked for waits for the user's 蝜潛?; only a pause the collector took by
     * itself (locked phone, finger on the screen) gives up after a while.
     */
    fun pauseTimesOut(pauseReason: String?): Boolean =
        pauseReason != CollectorInterruption.REASON_USER_REQUESTED &&
            pauseReason != CollectorInterruption.REASON_USER_LEFT

    /**
     * Whether one Back after a redirect already left the store sheet and put
     * the reward app (and the ad inside it) back in front. Then the app must
     * not be relaunched: that drops the ad and its reward.
     */
    fun backReturnedToApp(foregroundAfterBack: String?, appPackage: String): Boolean =
        foregroundAfterBack?.trim() == appPackage

    fun shouldStartNext(
        stopRequested: Boolean,
        previousEndReason: String?,
        keyguardLocked: Boolean
    ): Boolean {
        if (stopRequested) return false
        if (keyguardLocked) return false
        return previousEndReason == null || previousEndReason !in STOPPING_REASONS
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import java.time.Instant
import java.time.LocalTime
import java.time.ZoneId
import java.time.ZonedDateTime

/**
 * One daily collection time (asked by the user, 2026-11-15): at [hour]:[minute]
 * every day, run [appKeys] in order. Several entries may exist, each with its
 * own apps and its own on/off switch.
 */
data class ScheduleEntry(
    val id: Long,
    val hour: Int,
    val minute: Int,
    val appKeys: List<String>,
    val enabled: Boolean = true
) {
    val timeText: String get() = "%02d:%02d".format(hour, minute)
}

/** A schedule that came due and has not started yet (phone locked, or in use). */
data class PendingRun(
    val entryId: Long,
    val dueAt: Long,
    val appKeys: List<String>,
    /** A scan (count only) rather than a collection. */
    val scan: Boolean = false,
    /** Dropped this long after [dueAt] if it never got to start. */
    val graceMillis: Long = ScheduleMath.GRACE_MILLIS
)

/**
 * When to scan the apps for rewards still waiting (2026-11-15): every
 * [intervalHours] on the hour, or at fixed [times]; [MODE_OFF] scans never.
 */
data class ScanConfig(
    val mode: Int = MODE_OFF,
    val intervalHours: Int = 3,
    val appKeys: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val times: List<Pair<Int, Int>> = emptyList(),
    /** False until the user picks apps: an empty list then means "all". */
    val appsChosen: Boolean = false
) {
    /** The scan times as entries the schedule math understands. */
    fun entries(): List<ScheduleEntry> = when (mode) {
        MODE_INTERVAL -> (0 until 24 step intervalHours.coerceIn(1, 24)).map { h ->
            ScheduleEntry(SCAN_ID_BASE - h, h, 0, appKeys)
        }
        MODE_FIXED -> times.map { (h, m) -> ScheduleEntry(SCAN_ID_BASE - 100 - h * 60 - m, h, m, appKeys) }
        else -> emptyList()
    }

    /** An interval scan is replaced by the next one; a fixed one waits the usual time. */
    fun graceMillis(): Long =
        if (mode == MODE_INTERVAL) minOf(ScheduleMath.GRACE_MILLIS, intervalHours * 3_600_000L) else ScheduleMath.GRACE_MILLIS

    companion object {
        const val MODE_OFF = 0
        const val MODE_INTERVAL = 1
        const val MODE_FIXED = 2
        val INTERVALS = listOf(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12)
        private const val SCAN_ID_BASE = -1_000L

        fun encode(c: ScanConfig): String =
            "${c.mode}|${c.intervalHours}|${c.appKeys.joinToString(",")}|" +
                c.times.joinToString(",") { "%02d:%02d".format(it.first, it.second) } +
                "|${if (c.appsChosen) 1 else 0}"

        fun decode(raw: String?): ScanConfig {
            val parts = raw?.split("|") ?: return ScanConfig()
            if (parts.size != 4 && parts.size != 5) return ScanConfig()
            val times = parts[3].split(",").mapNotNull { t ->
                val hm = t.trim().split(":")
                val h = hm.getOrNull(0)?.toIntOrNull()?.takeIf { it in 0..23 }
                val m = hm.getOrNull(1)?.toIntOrNull()?.takeIf { it in 0..59 }
                if (h == null || m == null) null else h to m
            }.distinct().sortedWith(compareBy({ it.first }, { it.second }))
            val appKeys = parts[2].split(",").map { it.trim() }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
            return ScanConfig(
                mode = parts[0].toIntOrNull()?.takeIf { it in 0..2 } ?: MODE_OFF,
                intervalHours = parts[1].toIntOrNull()?.takeIf { it in 1..24 } ?: 3,
                appKeys = appKeys,
                times = times,
                // Old four-part records had no flag: a non-empty list was a
                // choice, an empty one still meant the default apps.
                appsChosen = if (parts.size == 5) parts[4] == "1" else appKeys.isNotEmpty()
            )
        }
    }
}

/**
 * Pure rules of the schedule, kept apart from AlarmManager and the service so
 * every decision has a JVM test.
 *
 * The collector can only act on a lit, unlocked screen with the reward app in
 * front (its taps go to the top window and OCR reads what is shown), and an
 * accessibility service cannot unlock a phone with a PIN. So a due schedule
 * does not start by itself on a locked phone: it waits, as the user chose,
 * until the phone is unlocked and nobody has used it for [IDLE_MILLIS], and is
 * dropped for the day after [GRACE_MILLIS].
 */
object ScheduleMath {

    /** A due schedule still starts this long after its time; later it is skipped. */
    const val GRACE_MILLIS = 3L * 60 * 60 * 1000

    /** Quiet time (no taps, scrolls or app switches) before a due schedule starts. */
    const val IDLE_MILLIS = 3L * 60 * 1000

    /** The next time [entry] fires strictly after [now]. */
    fun nextOccurrence(entry: ScheduleEntry, now: Long, zone: ZoneId = ZoneId.systemDefault()): Long {
        val nowAt = Instant.ofEpochMilli(now).atZone(zone)
        var at = ZonedDateTime.of(nowAt.toLocalDate(), LocalTime.of(entry.hour, entry.minute), zone)
        if (!at.toInstant().isAfter(nowAt.toInstant())) {
            at = ZonedDateTime.of(nowAt.toLocalDate().plusDays(1), LocalTime.of(entry.hour, entry.minute), zone)
        }
        return at.toInstant().toEpochMilli()
    }

    /** The enabled entry that fires first after [now], with its time; null when none. */
    fun nextDue(entries: List<ScheduleEntry>, now: Long, zone: ZoneId = ZoneId.systemDefault()): Pair<ScheduleEntry, Long>? =
        entries.filter { it.enabled && it.appKeys.isNotEmpty() }
            .map { it to nextOccurrence(it, now, zone) }
            .minByOrNull { it.second }

    enum class Decision {
        /** Start the run now. */
        START,
        /** The phone is locked (or the screen is off): wait for the user to unlock. */
        WAIT_UNLOCK,
        /** Unlocked, but someone used the phone within [IDLE_MILLIS]. */
        WAIT_IDLE,
        /** Another collection is already running; start after it. */
        WAIT_BUSY,
        /** Past [GRACE_MILLIS]: skip it for today. */
        EXPIRED
    }

    /**
     * What a pending run does now.
     *
     * @param idleSince latest of: the last real tap/scroll/app switch, the
     *   moment the phone was unlocked, and the due time (a schedule never starts
     *   on activity older than itself).
     */
    fun decide(
        pending: PendingRun,
        now: Long,
        locked: Boolean,
        screenOn: Boolean,
        collectorRunning: Boolean,
        idleSince: Long
    ): Decision = when {
        now - pending.dueAt > pending.graceMillis -> Decision.EXPIRED
        collectorRunning -> Decision.WAIT_BUSY
        locked || !screenOn -> Decision.WAIT_UNLOCK
        now - maxOf(idleSince, pending.dueAt) < IDLE_MILLIS -> Decision.WAIT_IDLE
        else -> Decision.START
    }

    /** Milliseconds left in a [Decision.WAIT_IDLE]. */
    fun idleRemaining(pending: PendingRun, now: Long, idleSince: Long): Long =
        (IDLE_MILLIS - (now - maxOf(idleSince, pending.dueAt))).coerceAtLeast(0L)

    /** "BITWALK?AHAGO" for the apps of an entry (unknown keys are skipped). */
    fun appsLabel(appKeys: List<String>): String {
        val names = appKeys.mapNotNull { CollectorProfiles.byKey(it)?.name }
        return if (names.isEmpty()) "嚗???App嚗? else names.joinToString("??)
    }

    // ---- storage format: one entry per line, "id|hour|minute|enabled|key,key" ----
    // Plain text instead of org.json: org.json is a stub in the JVM unit tests.

    fun encode(entries: List<ScheduleEntry>): String = entries.joinToString("\n") {
        "${it.id}|${it.hour}|${it.minute}|${if (it.enabled) 1 else 0}|${it.appKeys.joinToString(",")}"
    }

    fun decode(raw: String?): List<ScheduleEntry> = raw.orEmpty().lines().mapNotNull { line ->
        val parts = line.trim().split("|")
        if (parts.size != 5) return@mapNotNull null
        val id = parts[0].toLongOrNull() ?: return@mapNotNull null
        val hour = parts[1].toIntOrNull()?.takeIf { it in 0..23 } ?: return@mapNotNull null
        val minute = parts[2].toIntOrNull()?.takeIf { it in 0..59 } ?: return@mapNotNull null
        val keys = parts[4].split(",").map { it.trim() }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        ScheduleEntry(id, hour, minute, keys, parts[3] == "1")
    }.sortedWith(compareBy({ it.hour }, { it.minute }))

    fun encodePending(p: PendingRun): String =
        "${p.entryId}|${p.dueAt}|${p.appKeys.joinToString(",")}|${if (p.scan) 1 else 0}|${p.graceMillis}"

    fun decodePending(raw: String?): PendingRun? {
        val parts = raw?.split("|") ?: return null
        if (parts.size != 3 && parts.size != 5) return null
        val id = parts[0].toLongOrNull() ?: return null
        val due = parts[1].toLongOrNull() ?: return null
        val keys = parts[2].split(",").map { it.trim() }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        if (parts.size == 3) return PendingRun(id, due, keys)
        return PendingRun(id, due, keys, parts[3] == "1", parts[4].toLongOrNull() ?: GRACE_MILLIS)
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import android.app.AlarmManager
import android.app.NotificationChannel
import android.app.NotificationManager
import android.app.PendingIntent
import android.content.BroadcastReceiver
import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.os.Build
import android.util.Log
import androidx.core.app.NotificationCompat
import com.rewardadguard.app.service.RewardAdAccessibilityService
import com.rewardadguard.app.ui.MainActivity
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.StateFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asStateFlow

/**
 * Daily collection schedules (asked by the user, 2026-11-15).
 *
 * Entries and the one pending run live in SharedPreferences. One AlarmManager
 * alarm is kept for the earliest enabled entry; when it fires the run becomes
 * [pending] and the accessibility service's [ScheduledRunner] starts it once
 * the phone is unlocked and idle (see [ScheduleMath]). The alarm is set again
 * after every change, every alarm and every service (re)connect, so a reboot
 * or an app update re-arms it as soon as the accessibility service is back.
 */
object CollectorScheduler {

    private const val TAG = "CollectorScheduler"
    private const val PREFS = "collector_schedule"
    private const val KEY_ENTRIES = "entries"
    private const val KEY_PENDING = "pending"
    private const val KEY_SCAN = "scan"
    private const val EXTRA_SCAN = "scan"
    const val ACTION_ALARM = "com.rewardadguard.app.collector.SCHEDULE_ALARM"
    private const val EXTRA_ID = "entry_id"
    private const val EXTRA_DUE = "due_at"

    const val CHANNEL_ID = "collector_schedule"
    const val NOTIFICATION_ID = 4203

    private val _entries = MutableStateFlow<List<ScheduleEntry>>(emptyList())
    val entries: StateFlow<List<ScheduleEntry>> = _entries.asStateFlow()

    private val _scan = MutableStateFlow(ScanConfig())
    val scan: StateFlow<ScanConfig> = _scan.asStateFlow()

    private val _pending = MutableStateFlow<PendingRun?>(null)
    val pending: StateFlow<PendingRun?> = _pending.asStateFlow()

    /** What the waiting run is waiting for, for the UI ("蝑?閫??" ...). */
    private val _status = MutableStateFlow<String?>(null)
    val status: StateFlow<String?> = _status.asStateFlow()

    @Volatile
    private var loaded = false

    private fun prefs(context: Context) =
        context.applicationContext.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)

    fun load(context: Context) {
        if (loaded) return
        synchronized(this) {
            if (loaded) return
            val p = prefs(context)
            _entries.value = ScheduleMath.decode(p.getString(KEY_ENTRIES, null))
            _pending.value = ScheduleMath.decodePending(p.getString(KEY_PENDING, null))
            _scan.value = ScanConfig.decode(p.getString(KEY_SCAN, null))
            loaded = true
        }
    }

    fun save(context: Context, entries: List<ScheduleEntry>) {
        load(context)
        val sorted = ScheduleMath.decode(ScheduleMath.encode(entries))
        prefs(context).edit().putString(KEY_ENTRIES, ScheduleMath.encode(sorted)).apply()
        _entries.value = sorted
        reschedule(context)
    }

    fun upsert(context: Context, entry: ScheduleEntry) {
        load(context)
        save(context, _entries.value.filterNot { it.id == entry.id } + entry)
    }

    fun remove(context: Context, id: Long) {
        load(context)
        save(context, _entries.value.filterNot { it.id == id })
        if (_pending.value?.entryId == id) clearPending(context, null)
    }

    fun saveScan(context: Context, config: ScanConfig) {
        load(context)
        prefs(context).edit().putString(KEY_SCAN, ScanConfig.encode(config)).apply()
        _scan.value = config
        reschedule(context)
    }

    internal fun setPending(context: Context, run: PendingRun) {
        prefs(context).edit().putString(KEY_PENDING, ScheduleMath.encodePending(run)).apply()
        _pending.value = run
    }

    /** Drops the pending run; [message] leaves a closing notification when set. */
    fun clearPending(context: Context, message: String?) {
        prefs(context).edit().remove(KEY_PENDING).apply()
        _pending.value = null
        _status.value = null
        val manager = context.getSystemService(NotificationManager::class.java) ?: return
        if (message == null) {
            manager.cancel(NOTIFICATION_ID)
        } else {
            notify(context, "???嗅?", message, ongoing = false)
        }
    }

    internal fun setStatus(context: Context, text: String?) {
        if (_status.value == text) return
        _status.value = text
        val run = _pending.value ?: return
        if (text != null) {
            val what = if (run.scan) "????" else "???嗅?"
            notify(context, "${what}蝑?銝哨?${timeOf(run)}嚗?, "$text??{ScheduleMath.appsLabel(run.appKeys)}", ongoing = true)
        }
    }

    private fun timeOf(run: PendingRun): String =
        (_entries.value + _scan.value.entries()).firstOrNull { it.id == run.entryId }?.timeText ?: "??"

    /** Sets (or cancels) the alarms: one for the collection schedules, one for the scans. */
    fun reschedule(context: Context) {
        load(context)
        arm(context, requestCode = 0, entries = _entries.value, scan = false)
        arm(context, requestCode = 1, entries = _scan.value.entries(), scan = true)
    }

    private fun arm(context: Context, requestCode: Int, entries: List<ScheduleEntry>, scan: Boolean) {
        val alarms = context.getSystemService(AlarmManager::class.java) ?: return
        val next = ScheduleMath.nextDue(entries, System.currentTimeMillis())
        val intent = Intent(context, ScheduleAlarmReceiver::class.java).setAction(ACTION_ALARM)
        if (next == null) {
            alarms.cancel(PendingIntent.getBroadcast(context, requestCode, intent, PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT or PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE))
            return
        }
        val (entry, at) = next
        intent.putExtra(EXTRA_ID, entry.id).putExtra(EXTRA_DUE, at).putExtra(EXTRA_SCAN, scan)
        val operation = PendingIntent.getBroadcast(
            context, requestCode, intent, PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT or PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE
        )
        runCatching {
            if (canExact(alarms)) {
                alarms.setExactAndAllowWhileIdle(AlarmManager.RTC_WAKEUP, at, operation)
            } else {
                // Without the exact-alarm grant Doze may deliver this some
                // minutes late; the run waits for an idle phone anyway.
                alarms.setAndAllowWhileIdle(AlarmManager.RTC_WAKEUP, at, operation)
            }
        }.onFailure { Log.w(TAG, "alarm not set", it) }
    }

    fun canExact(context: Context): Boolean =
        context.getSystemService(AlarmManager::class.java)?.let { canExact(it) } ?: false

    private fun canExact(alarms: AlarmManager): Boolean =
        Build.VERSION.SDK_INT < Build.VERSION_CODES.S || alarms.canScheduleExactAlarms()

    internal fun onAlarm(context: Context, entryId: Long, dueAt: Long, scan: Boolean) {
        load(context)
        val entry = (if (scan) _scan.value.entries() else _entries.value).firstOrNull { it.id == entryId && it.enabled }
        val waiting = _pending.value
        // A collection still waiting is never pushed aside by a scan; a newer
        // due run otherwise replaces the older one.
        if (entry != null && !(scan && waiting != null && !waiting.scan)) {
            setPending(
                context,
                PendingRun(entry.id, dueAt, entry.appKeys, scan, if (scan) _scan.value.graceMillis() else ScheduleMath.GRACE_MILLIS)
            )
            setStatus(context, null)
            setStatus(context, "???唬?嚗???憪?)
            RewardAdAccessibilityService.instance?.collectorScheduledRunner()?.kick()
        }
        reschedule(context)
    }

    private fun notify(context: Context, title: String, text: String, ongoing: Boolean) {
        val manager = context.getSystemService(NotificationManager::class.java) ?: return
        if (manager.getNotificationChannel(CHANNEL_ID) == null) {
            manager.createNotificationChannel(
                NotificationChannel(CHANNEL_ID, "???嗅?", NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_DEFAULT).apply {
                    description = "?????唬???敺圾???蔭????"
                    setShowBadge(false)
                }
            )
        }
        val open = PendingIntent.getActivity(
            context, 0,
            Intent(context, MainActivity::class.java).addFlags(Intent.FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK),
            PendingIntent.FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT or PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE
        )
        val builder = NotificationCompat.Builder(context, CHANNEL_ID)
            .setSmallIcon(android.R.drawable.ic_lock_idle_alarm)
            .setContentTitle(title)
            .setContentText(text)
            .setStyle(NotificationCompat.BigTextStyle().bigText(text))
            .setContentIntent(open)
            .setOngoing(ongoing)
            .setOnlyAlertOnce(true)
            .setAutoCancel(!ongoing)
        runCatching { manager.notify(NOTIFICATION_ID, builder.build()) }
    }

    internal fun entryId(intent: Intent) = intent.getLongExtra(EXTRA_ID, -1L)
    internal fun dueAt(intent: Intent) = intent.getLongExtra(EXTRA_DUE, System.currentTimeMillis())
    internal fun isScan(intent: Intent) = intent.getBooleanExtra(EXTRA_SCAN, false)
}

/** The schedule's alarm. */
class ScheduleAlarmReceiver : BroadcastReceiver() {
    override fun onReceive(context: Context, intent: Intent) {
        if (intent.action != CollectorScheduler.ACTION_ALARM) return
        CollectorScheduler.onAlarm(
            context.applicationContext,
            CollectorScheduler.entryId(intent),
            CollectorScheduler.dueAt(intent),
            CollectorScheduler.isScan(intent)
        )
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

/**
 * Who is allowed to act on the screen right now (integration plan 禮3).
 *
 * Held by [com.rewardadguard.app.service.RewardAdAccessibilityService] and read
 * by the guard on its event path. It is intentionally a plain enum with no
 * Android dependency: the mutual-exclusion rule is the most safety-critical
 * part of the integration and must be testable on the JVM.
 */
enum class CollectorState {
    /** No collection run: the guard behaves exactly as it did before. */
    IDLE,

    /** The collector owns the screen; the guard only observes and logs. */
    RUNNING,

    /** The collector is paused (lock screen, user touch): the guard resumes. */
    PAUSED
}

/**
 * The guard's side of the mutual-exclusion contract.
 *
 * Only [CollectorState.RUNNING] takes the screen away from the guard. While the
 * collector is [CollectorState.PAUSED] nobody is driving the collector, so the
 * guard's passive protection must keep working - pausing the collector must
 * never leave the user unprotected.
 */
object GuardYield {

    fun shouldGuardAct(state: CollectorState): Boolean = state != CollectorState.RUNNING

    /** Message written when the guard steps aside, for the event log. */
    fun yieldMessage(what: String): String = "guard skipped $what and left it to the collector"
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import android.content.Context
import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.BitmapFactory
import kotlin.math.roundToInt

/**
 * Loads pc-collector's three corner templates from `assets/templates` and runs
 * [CornerGlyphMatcher] on a screenshot.
 *
 * The images are the same files the PC script uses (`close_circle.png`,
 * `next_circle.png`, `back_arrow.png`), copied verbatim. Keeping one source of
 * truth means a template improved on the PC can be dropped in here without
 * retuning the threshold.
 *
 * Android-only because decoding a PNG needs `BitmapFactory`; the matching
 * itself stays in the pure Kotlin class so the tests do not need a device.
 */
class CornerGlyphDetector(private val context: Context) {

    private val templates: List<GlyphTemplate> by lazy { loadTemplates() }

    fun find(screenshot: Bitmap): List<GlyphHit> {
        if (screenshot.width <= 0 || screenshot.height <= 0) return emptyList()
        return CornerGlyphMatcher(templates).find(grayImage(screenshot))
    }

    /**
     * Per corner region, the best score of every template, plus where it was.
     * The debug command reports this so a field run shows *why* nothing matched
     * (e.g. "best 0.61, below 0.78") instead of an empty list.
     */
    fun bestPerRegion(screenshot: Bitmap): List<RegionBest> {
        val gray = grayImage(screenshot)
        val matcher = CornerGlyphMatcher(templates, threshold = 0.0)
        val hits = matcher.find(gray)
        val regions = CornerGeometry.cornerRegions(gray.width, gray.height)
        return regions.mapIndexed { index, region ->
            val best = hits.filter { it.regionIndex == index }.maxByOrNull { it.score }
            RegionBest(regionIndex = index, region = region, hit = best)
        }
    }

    /** The install card's "??, searched only in the region above "Install". */
    fun findBackArrow(screenshot: Bitmap, region: Box): GlyphHit? {
        val template = templates.firstOrNull { it.kind == "back" } ?: return null
        return CornerGlyphMatcher(templates).findInRegion(grayImage(screenshot), template, region, 0.85)
    }

    private fun loadTemplates(): List<GlyphTemplate> = TEMPLATE_FILES.mapNotNull { (kind, path) ->
        runCatching {
            context.assets.open(path).use { stream ->
                val bitmap = BitmapFactory.decodeStream(stream) ?: return@use null
                GlyphTemplate(kind, grayImage(bitmap), fromScreenTop = path in FROM_SCREEN_TOP)
            }
        }.getOrNull()
    }

    private fun grayImage(bitmap: Bitmap): GrayImage {
        val width = bitmap.width
        val height = bitmap.height
        val pixels = IntArray(width * height)
        bitmap.getPixels(pixels, 0, width, 0, 0, width, height)
        val gray = ByteArray(width * height)
        for (index in pixels.indices) {
            val color = pixels[index]
            val r = (color shr 16) and 0xFF
            val g = (color shr 8) and 0xFF
            val b = color and 0xFF
            // ITU-R BT.601 weights, the same luminance OpenCV's IMREAD_GRAYSCALE
            // uses, so scores stay comparable with the PC recordings.
            val luma = (0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b).roundToInt().coerceIn(0, 255)
            gray[index] = luma.toByte()
        }
        return GrayImage(width, height, gray)
    }

    companion object {
        private val FROM_SCREEN_TOP = setOf(
            "templates/chevron_circle.png",
            "templates/thin_chevron.png",
            "templates/thin_close.png"
        )

        private val TEMPLATE_FILES = listOf(
            "next" to "templates/next_circle.png",
            // The bare "?閏" skip of InMobi / Fyber ads, cut from a BITWALK
            // screen (2026-11-13 14:55) where nothing else could close it.
            "next" to "templates/skip_bar.png",
            // Mintegral's ">" in a dark circle, the only way out of its
            // playable "WI-FI ?" ad (BITWALK, 2026-11-13 16:58).
            "next" to "templates/chevron_circle.png",
            // Mintegral's thin ">" and thin "X" with no circle, level with the
            // status bar (y ~ 88): BITWALK's MBRewardVideoActivity waited for
            // them until it timed out, again and again (2026-11-16 11:28).
            "next" to "templates/thin_chevron.png",
            "close" to "templates/close_circle.png",
            "close" to "templates/thin_close.png",
            // InMobi's "Ad 2 of 2" card: a dark X in a thin dark ring on white,
            // top left below the progress bars (BITWALK, 2026-11-17 09:20);
            // the white-on-dark close_circle scored nothing there.
            "close" to "templates/outline_close.png",
            "back" to "templates/back_arrow.png"
        )
    }
}

/** Best template match in one corner region; [hit] is null when none scored. */
data class RegionBest(val regionIndex: Int, val region: Box, val hit: GlyphHit?)

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\collector\CornerGlyphMatcher.kt

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import kotlin.math.max
import kotlin.math.min
import kotlin.math.roundToInt
import kotlin.math.sqrt

/**
 * An 8-bit grayscale image held in a byte array, row major.
 *
 * Template matching is deliberately independent of Android and of any imaging
 * library (integration plan 禮2: no OpenCV, ~30 MB saved). Everything the
 * matcher needs is `width`, `height` and the pixels, so the same code runs on a
 * phone screenshot and on a synthetic array in a JVM test.
 */
class GrayImage(val width: Int, val height: Int, val pixels: ByteArray) {

    init {
        require(width > 0 && height > 0) { "image must not be empty" }
        require(pixels.size >= width * height) { "pixel buffer is smaller than the image" }
    }

    /** Luminance of one pixel, 0..255. */
    fun at(x: Int, y: Int): Int = pixels[y * width + x].toInt() and 0xFF

    /**
     * Bilinear resize. Used for the template pyramid; screenshots are shrunk
     * with [downscaled] instead, because averaging is the right filter when
     * throwing pixels away.
     */
    fun resized(targetWidth: Int, targetHeight: Int): GrayImage {
        val w = targetWidth.coerceAtLeast(1)
        val h = targetHeight.coerceAtLeast(1)
        if (w == width && h == height) return this
        val out = ByteArray(w * h)
        val scaleX = width.toDouble() / w
        val scaleY = height.toDouble() / h
        for (y in 0 until h) {
            val sourceY = ((y + 0.5) * scaleY - 0.5).coerceIn(0.0, (height - 1).toDouble())
            val y0 = sourceY.toInt()
            val y1 = min(y0 + 1, height - 1)
            val fy = sourceY - y0
            for (x in 0 until w) {
                val sourceX = ((x + 0.5) * scaleX - 0.5).coerceIn(0.0, (width - 1).toDouble())
                val x0 = sourceX.toInt()
                val x1 = min(x0 + 1, width - 1)
                val fx = sourceX - x0
                val top = at(x0, y0) * (1 - fx) + at(x1, y0) * fx
                val bottom = at(x0, y1) * (1 - fx) + at(x1, y1) * fx
                out[y * w + x] = (top * (1 - fy) + bottom * fy).roundToInt().coerceIn(0, 255).toByte()
            }
        }
        return GrayImage(w, h, out)
    }

    /** Box-average downscale by an integer factor; the cheap pyramid level. */
    fun downscaled(factor: Int): GrayImage {
        if (factor <= 1) return this
        val w = max(1, width / factor)
        val h = max(1, height / factor)
        val out = ByteArray(w * h)
        for (y in 0 until h) {
            for (x in 0 until w) {
                var sum = 0
                var count = 0
                val baseY = y * factor
                val baseX = x * factor
                for (dy in 0 until factor) {
                    val sy = baseY + dy
                    if (sy >= height) break
                    val row = sy * width
                    for (dx in 0 until factor) {
                        val sx = baseX + dx
                        if (sx >= width) break
                        sum += pixels[row + sx].toInt() and 0xFF
                        count++
                    }
                }
                out[y * w + x] = (sum / max(1, count)).toByte()
            }
        }
        return GrayImage(w, h, out)
    }

    companion object {
        fun filled(width: Int, height: Int, value: Int): GrayImage =
            GrayImage(width, height, ByteArray(width * height) { value.coerceIn(0, 255).toByte() })
    }
}

/** A template and what glyph it represents ("close", "next", "back"). */
/**
 * [fromScreenTop]: search the top-right corner from y = 0 instead of below the
 * status bar. Only for large, distinctive glyphs (Mintegral's ">" circle sits
 * at y = 45..134); small ones would match status-bar icons.
 */
data class GlyphTemplate(val kind: String, val image: GrayImage, val fromScreenTop: Boolean = false)

/** One template match: where it was found and with what confidence. */
data class GlyphHit(
    val kind: String,
    val regionIndex: Int,
    val score: Double,
    val bounds: Box
)

/**
 * Corner button templates (`X`, `>>`, `<-`) ported from pc-collector.
 *
 * Why only the corners: matching the whole screen tapped ad artwork and opened
 * the store (11-09 and 11-11 field runs). pc-collector restricts the same
 * search to the top-left and top-right bands, and this class keeps those exact
 * proportions ([CornerGeometry.cornerRegions]) so a threshold tuned there
 * still means the same thing here.
 *
 * Matching is zero-mean normalised cross-correlation, the pure-Kotlin
 * equivalent of OpenCV's `TM_CCOEFF_NORMED`. It is scale invariant (unlike
 * squared difference) and answers "the same shape?" rather than "the same
 * brightness?", which is what makes one template work across ad SDKs.
 *
 * A coarse pass on a 4x downscaled image, then a local full-resolution
 * refinement, keeps a 56x56 template search fast enough to run on every ad
 * frame without a native library.
 */
class CornerGlyphMatcher(
    private val templates: List<GlyphTemplate>,
    private val threshold: Double = CornerGeometry.THRESHOLD
) {

    private data class Candidate(val x: Int, val y: Int, val score: Double)

    fun find(image: GrayImage): List<GlyphHit> {
        val regions = CornerGeometry.cornerRegions(image.width, image.height)
        if (regions.isEmpty() || templates.isEmpty()) return emptyList()

        val shortSide = min(image.width, image.height)
        val base = shortSide.toDouble() / CornerGeometry.TEMPLATE_BASE_WIDTH
        val downscale = if (shortSide >= COARSE_DOWNSCALE_MIN_SIDE) COARSE_DOWNSCALE else 1
        val small = if (downscale > 1) image.downscaled(downscale) else image

        val found = ArrayList<GlyphHit>()
        for (template in templates) {
            for (factor in SCALES) {
                val fullSize = max(12, (template.image.width * base * factor).roundToInt())
                if (fullSize >= image.width || fullSize >= image.height) continue
                val full = Prepared(template.image.resized(fullSize, fullSize))
                val coarseSize = max(8, fullSize / downscale)
                val coarse = if (downscale > 1) {
                    Prepared(full.image.resized(coarseSize, coarseSize))
                } else {
                    full
                }

                for ((regionIndex, cornerRegion) in regions.withIndex()) {
                    // `>>` skip arrows only ever sit top-right (vision.py).
                    if (template.kind == "next" && regionIndex == 1) continue
                    val region = if (template.fromScreenTop && regionIndex == 0) {
                        Box(cornerRegion.left, 0, cornerRegion.right, cornerRegion.bottom)
                    } else {
                        cornerRegion
                    }
                    val regionBox = if (downscale > 1) {
                        Box(
                            region.left / downscale,
                            region.top / downscale,
                            region.right / downscale,
                            region.bottom / downscale
                        )
                    } else {
                        region
                    }
                    val coarseHit = best(small, coarse, regionBox, if (downscale > 1) 2 else 1) ?: continue
                    val refined = if (downscale > 1) {
                        val startX = coarseHit.x * downscale
                        val startY = coarseHit.y * downscale
                        val pad = downscale * 2
                        val window = Box(
                            max(0, startX - pad),
                            max(0, startY - pad),
                            min(image.width, startX + fullSize + pad),
                            min(image.height, startY + fullSize + pad)
                        )
                        best(image, full, window, 1)
                    } else {
                        coarseHit
                    } ?: continue

                    if (refined.score < threshold) continue
                    found.add(
                        GlyphHit(
                            kind = template.kind,
                            regionIndex = regionIndex,
                            score = refined.score,
                            bounds = Box(refined.x, refined.y, refined.x + fullSize, refined.y + fullSize)
                        )
                    )
                }
            }
        }

        // One button per area: the same X is often matched by two scales.
        val result = ArrayList<GlyphHit>()
        for (hit in found.sortedByDescending { it.score }) {
            val duplicate = result.any {
                kotlin.math.abs(it.bounds.centerX - hit.bounds.centerX) < DUPLICATE_RADIUS_PX &&
                    kotlin.math.abs(it.bounds.centerY - hit.bounds.centerY) < DUPLICATE_RADIUS_PX
            }
            if (!duplicate) result.add(hit)
        }
        return result
    }

    /**
     * Best match of [template] inside an arbitrary region (the "?? of an
     * install card). pc-collector's `find_template` uses 0.85/1.0/1.15 scales
     * and a 0.85 threshold with no corner restriction; the same coarse pass and
     * local refinement keep it affordable on a phone.
     */
    fun findInRegion(
        image: GrayImage,
        template: GlyphTemplate,
        region: Box,
        threshold: Double = 0.85
    ): GlyphHit? {
        if (region.width <= 0 || region.height <= 0) return null
        val factor = when {
            region.area >= 200_000 -> 4
            region.area >= 40_000 -> 2
            else -> 1
        }
        val small = if (factor > 1) image.downscaled(factor) else image
        val smallRegion = Box(
            region.left / factor,
            region.top / factor,
            region.right / factor,
            region.bottom / factor
        )
        var bestHit: Candidate? = null
        var bestSize = 0
        for (scale in SCALES) {
            val size = max(12, (template.image.width * scale).roundToInt())
            if (size >= image.width || size >= image.height) continue
            val full = Prepared(template.image.resized(size, size))
            val coarse = if (factor > 1) {
                Prepared(full.image.resized(max(8, size / factor), max(8, size / factor)))
            } else {
                full
            }
            val coarseHit = best(small, coarse, smallRegion, 2) ?: continue
            val startX = coarseHit.x * factor
            val startY = coarseHit.y * factor
            val pad = factor * 2
            val window = Box(
                max(0, startX - pad),
                max(0, startY - pad),
                min(image.width, startX + size + pad),
                min(image.height, startY + size + pad)
            )
            val refined = best(image, full, window, 1) ?: continue
            if (bestHit == null || refined.score > bestHit.score) {
                bestHit = refined
                bestSize = size
            }
        }
        val hit = bestHit ?: return null
        if (hit.score < threshold) return null
        return GlyphHit(template.kind, -1, hit.score, Box(hit.x, hit.y, hit.x + bestSize, hit.y + bestSize))
    }

    /** Highest NCC score inside [region], or null when the template cannot fit. */
    private fun best(image: GrayImage, template: Prepared, region: Box, stride: Int): Candidate? {
        val maxX = region.right - template.width
        val maxY = region.bottom - template.height
        if (maxX < region.left || maxY < region.top) return null
        var bestX = region.left
        var bestY = region.top
        var bestScore = -1.0
        var y = region.top
        while (y <= maxY) {
            var x = region.left
            while (x <= maxX) {
                val score = template.scoreAt(image, x, y)
                if (score > bestScore) {
                    bestScore = score
                    bestX = x
                    bestY = y
                }
                x += stride
            }
            y += stride
        }
        return Candidate(bestX, bestY, bestScore)
    }

    /** A template plus the sums NCC needs, computed once per scale. */
    private class Prepared(val image: GrayImage) {

        val width: Int = image.width
        val height: Int = image.height
        private val count: Double = (width * height).toDouble()
        private val sum: Double
        private val variance: Double

        init {
            var s = 0.0
            var sq = 0.0
            for (y in 0 until height) {
                for (x in 0 until width) {
                    val value = image.at(x, y).toDouble()
                    s += value
                    sq += value * value
                }
            }
            sum = s
            variance = sq - (s * s) / count
        }

        /**
         * Zero-mean normalised cross-correlation of this template with the
         * image window at (originX, originY). A flat window or flat template has
         * no shape and scores 0 instead of dividing by zero.
         */
        fun scoreAt(image: GrayImage, originX: Int, originY: Int): Double {
            var sumImage = 0.0
            var sumImageSq = 0.0
            var sumProduct = 0.0
            for (ty in 0 until height) {
                val row = (originY + ty) * image.width + originX
                val templateRow = ty * width
                for (tx in 0 until width) {
                    val pixel = (image.pixels[row + tx].toInt() and 0xFF).toDouble()
                    val templatePixel = (this.image.pixels[templateRow + tx].toInt() and 0xFF).toDouble()
                    sumImage += pixel
                    sumImageSq += pixel * pixel
                    sumProduct += pixel * templatePixel
                }
            }
            val imageVariance = sumImageSq - (sumImage * sumImage) / count
            if (imageVariance <= 1e-6 || variance <= 1e-6) return 0.0
            val covariance = sumProduct - (sumImage * sum) / count
            return covariance / sqrt(imageVariance * variance)
        }
    }

    companion object {
        /** Threshold from pc-collector's `CORNER_THRESHOLD`. */
        private const val DUPLICATE_RADIUS_PX = 40
        private const val COARSE_DOWNSCALE = 4
        private const val COARSE_DOWNSCALE_MIN_SIDE = 600
        private val SCALES = doubleArrayOf(0.85, 1.0, 1.15)
    }
}

/**
 * Where ad SDKs put their close / skip controls, copied from
 * `reward_collector/vision.py:corner_regions`.
 *
 * The numbers are empirical, not aesthetic: the right box starts below the
 * status bar because its icons produced false matches there, the left box
 * starts at y=0 because full-screen ads put their X at (37,37), and both reach
 * 22% down because a card interstitial had its X at (86,510).
 */
object CornerGeometry {

    const val TEMPLATE_BASE_WIDTH = 1220.0
    const val THRESHOLD = 0.78

    fun cornerRegions(width: Int, height: Int): List<Box> {
        if (width <= 0 || height <= 0) return emptyList()
        val portrait = height >= width
        val top = (height * (if (portrait) 0.035 else 0.0)).toInt()
        val bottom = (height * (if (portrait) 0.22 else 0.25)).toInt()
        val side = (width * 0.40).toInt()
        return listOf(
            Box(width - side, top, width, bottom),
            Box(0, 0, side, bottom)
        )
    }
}
