package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService
import android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService.TakeScreenshotCallback
import android.accessibilityservice.AccessibilityService.ScreenshotResult
import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.Rect
import android.os.Build
import android.os.SystemClock
import android.view.Display
import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityNodeInfo
import androidx.annotation.RequiresApi
import com.google.mlkit.vision.common.InputImage
import com.google.mlkit.vision.text.TextRecognition
import com.google.mlkit.vision.text.TextRecognizer
import com.google.mlkit.vision.text.chinese.ChineseTextRecognizerOptions
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.suspendCancellableCoroutine
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.coroutines.withTimeoutOrNull
import java.util.concurrent.ExecutorService
import java.util.concurrent.Executors
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean
import kotlin.coroutines.resume

/** A screenshot plus how long taking it took, or why it failed. */
data class ScreenCapture(val bitmap: Bitmap?, val elapsedMillis: Long, val error: String?)

/** A [Snapshot] together with the pixels it came from (debug entry point only). */
data class ScreenReading(val snapshot: Snapshot, val bitmap: Bitmap?)

/**
 * A reading with the corner template results the ad handler needs. The caller
 * owns [bitmap] and must close this object, which recycles it.
 */
class ScreenAnalysis(
    val snapshot: Snapshot,
    val bitmap: Bitmap?,
    val corners: List<GlyphHit>,
    val backArrow: GlyphHit?
) : java.io.Closeable {
    private var closed = false

    /** Safe to call more than once (afterReward closes early, then in finally). */
    override fun close() {
        if (closed) return
        closed = true
        bitmap?.recycle()
    }
}

/**
 * Reads the current screen into a [Snapshot].
 *
 * Two sources, in this order:
 *  1. the accessibility node tree - BitWalk is Flutter and exposes semantics, so
 *     "?臬???50 ?蝡? is readable without waiting for the screen to settle;
 *  2. ML Kit Chinese OCR on a screenshot, as a fallback for ad SDKs that draw
 *     their text into a canvas/WebView where no node exists.
 *
 * Heavy work (a screenshot binder call plus OCR) happens only when the
 * collector asks for it. Nothing here is wired into `onAccessibilityEvent`; the
 * plan's "cheap callbacks" rule still holds.
 *
 * OCR is Android 11+ only (`AccessibilityService.takeScreenshot`). On older
 * devices the node tree is used alone and [isOcrSupported] stays false, which
 * the UI is expected to surface as "甇方?蝵桐??舀 OCR".
 */
class ScreenReader(private val service: AccessibilityService) {

    private val recognizer: TextRecognizer by lazy {
        TextRecognition.getClient(ChineseTextRecognizerOptions.Builder().build())
    }

    private var recognizerCreated = false

    /**
     * Delivers screenshot callbacks off the main looper: `onSuccess` copies a
     * full-screen hardware buffer into an ARGB bitmap (~10+ MB), which is far
     * too heavy to do on the service's main thread on every ad frame.
     */
    private val screenshotPool: ExecutorService by lazy {
        Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor { runnable ->
            Thread(runnable, "collector-screenshot").apply { isDaemon = true }
        }
    }
    private var screenshotPoolCreated = false

    /** Loaded once: decoding the three template PNGs per ad frame would be waste. */
    private val cornerDetector by lazy { CornerGlyphDetector(service) }

    @Volatile
    private var lastScreenshotAt = -1L

    fun isOcrSupported(): Boolean = Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.R

    /**
     * Reads the screen. The caller owns the returned bitmap in [ScreenReading];
     * [read] is the convenience wrapper that recycles it.
     */
    suspend fun readDetailed(
        foregroundPackage: String? = null,
        foregroundActivity: String? = null,
        includeOcr: Boolean = true
    ): ScreenReading {
        val capture = if (includeOcr && isOcrSupported()) captureScreen() else null
        val bitmap = capture?.bitmap

        val disabledNodes = ArrayList<Box>()
        val nodes = withContext(Dispatchers.Default) { collectNodeBoxes(disabledNodes) }

        var ocrBoxes: List<TextBox> = emptyList()
        var ocrMillis = 0L
        var ocrError = capture?.error
        if (includeOcr && !isOcrSupported()) {
            // The UI shows this verbatim, hence the zh-TW string: "this device
            // does not support OCR". The node tree still works.
            ocrError = "甇方?蝵桐??舀 OCR嚗?閬?Android 11 隞乩?嚗?
        }
        if (bitmap != null) {
            val started = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()
            try {
                ocrBoxes = withContext(Dispatchers.Default) { recognize(bitmap) }
            } catch (t: Throwable) {
                if (t is kotlinx.coroutines.CancellationException) throw t
                ocrError = "mlkit: ${t::class.java.simpleName}: ${t.message}"
            }
            ocrMillis = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - started
        }

        val metrics = service.resources.displayMetrics
        val width = bitmap?.width ?: metrics.widthPixels
        val height = bitmap?.height ?: metrics.heightPixels
        // The window actually on screen wins over the event-derived guess. On
        // 2026-11-12 a Back left LINE for HAHAGO without a window-state event,
        // the reported package stayed LINE, and the lottery wait pressed Back
        // and looked for X buttons on HAHAGO for four minutes.
        val rootPackage = runCatching { service.rootInActiveWindow?.packageName?.toString() }
            .getOrNull()
        val packageName = ForegroundResolver.packageName(rootPackage, foregroundPackage)
        val activityName = if (packageName == foregroundPackage) foregroundActivity else null

        if (bitmap != null && ocrBoxes.isNotEmpty()) {
            // Off unless the user switched on OCR calibration (2026-11-16).
            OcrCalibration.maybeSave(service, bitmap, ocrBoxes, packageName)
        }

        val snapshot = Snapshot(
            width = width,
            height = height,
            capturedAt = System.currentTimeMillis(),
            foregroundPackage = packageName,
            foregroundActivity = activityName,
            ocrSupported = isOcrSupported(),
            // The floating ?怠?/?迫 panel is ours, not the app's content.
            boxes = FloatingControls.withoutPanel(nodes + ocrBoxes),
            ocrMillis = ocrMillis,
            ocrError = ocrError,
            disabled = disabledNodes
        )
        return ScreenReading(snapshot, bitmap)
    }

    /** [readDetailed] and frees the screenshot; use this on the production path. */
    suspend fun read(
        foregroundPackage: String? = null,
        foregroundActivity: String? = null,
        includeOcr: Boolean = true
    ): Snapshot {
        val reading = readDetailed(foregroundPackage, foregroundActivity, includeOcr)
        reading.bitmap?.recycle()
        return reading.snapshot
    }

    /**
     * A reading plus the corner template matches, for the ad handler.
     *
     * [backArrowRegion] is evaluated on the snapshot and, when it returns a box,
     * the install-card "?? template is searched there. The caller must close the
     * result; that recycles the screenshot.
     */
    suspend fun analyze(
        foregroundPackage: String? = null,
        foregroundActivity: String? = null,
        backArrowRegion: ((Snapshot) -> Box?)? = null
    ): ScreenAnalysis {
        val reading = readDetailed(foregroundPackage, foregroundActivity)
        val bitmap = reading.bitmap ?: return ScreenAnalysis(reading.snapshot, null, emptyList(), null)
        try {
            val corners = cornerDetector.find(bitmap)
            val region = backArrowRegion?.invoke(reading.snapshot)
            val back = region?.let { cornerDetector.findBackArrow(bitmap, it) }
            return ScreenAnalysis(reading.snapshot, bitmap, corners, back)
        } catch (t: Throwable) {
            bitmap.recycle()
            throw t
        }
    }

    /**
     * Takes one screenshot. Every failure path returns a capture with a null
     * bitmap and a readable [ScreenCapture.error] instead of throwing: an ad
     * screen is exactly where the system is allowed to say "not now" (rate
     * limit) and the collector must fall back to the node tree, not crash.
     */
    suspend fun captureScreen(): ScreenCapture {
        if (!isOcrSupported()) {
            return ScreenCapture(null, 0L, "takeScreenshot needs Android 11 (API 30)")
        }
        // Android accepts one accessibility screenshot per ~333 ms and answers
        // a faster request with ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_INTERVAL_TIME_SHORT. Two
        // reads in a row (tab settle, then popup check) hit that on 2026-11-12:
        // the second reading had no OCR at all and BITWALK's 鞈箏? tab was
        // judged "no reward" on 12 nodes alone. Space requests out, and retry
        // once if the system still says too soon.
        ScreenshotPacing.waitMillis(lastScreenshotAt, SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()).let { wait ->
            if (wait > 0L) delay(wait)
        }
        var capture = captureOnce()
        if (capture.error?.contains("INTERVAL_TIME_SHORT") == true) {
            delay(ScreenshotPacing.MIN_INTERVAL_MILLIS)
            capture = captureOnce()
        }
        return capture
    }

    private suspend fun captureOnce(): ScreenCapture {
        lastScreenshotAt = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()
        return withContext(Dispatchers.Main) {
            // The system normally reports a rate limit through onFailure, but a
            // callback that never arrives would freeze the whole run forever
            // (observed 2026-11-12: no events after the first snapshot). A hard
            // timeout turns that into a node-only reading the engine can use.
            withTimeoutOrNull(SCREENSHOT_TIMEOUT_MILLIS) {
                takeScreenshotCompat()
            } ?: ScreenCapture(
                bitmap = null,
                elapsedMillis = SCREENSHOT_TIMEOUT_MILLIS,
                error = "screenshot callback timed out after ${SCREENSHOT_TIMEOUT_MILLIS}ms"
            )
        }
    }

    @RequiresApi(Build.VERSION_CODES.R)
    private suspend fun takeScreenshotCompat(): ScreenCapture {
        val started = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime()
        screenshotPoolCreated = true
        val resumed = AtomicBoolean(false)
        return suspendCancellableCoroutine { continuation ->
            // After the 5-second timeout cancels this wait, a late onSuccess
            // still copies a full-screen bitmap (~13 MB). Nobody would ever
            // receive it, so it is recycled instead of leaked (review P2-9).
            continuation.invokeOnCancellation { resumed.set(true) }
            fun finish(capture: ScreenCapture) {
                if (resumed.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
                    continuation.resume(capture)
                } else {
                    capture.bitmap?.recycle()
                }
            }
            try {
                service.takeScreenshot(
                    Display.DEFAULT_DISPLAY,
                    screenshotPool,
                    object : TakeScreenshotCallback {
                        override fun onSuccess(result: ScreenshotResult) {
                            val bitmap = try {
                                Bitmap.wrapHardwareBuffer(result.hardwareBuffer, result.colorSpace)
                                    ?.copy(Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888, false)
                            } catch (t: Throwable) {
                                null
                            } finally {
                                runCatching { result.hardwareBuffer.close() }
                            }
                            finish(
                                ScreenCapture(
                                    bitmap = bitmap,
                                    elapsedMillis = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - started,
                                    error = if (bitmap == null) "screenshot could not be copied to a bitmap" else null
                                )
                            )
                        }

                        override fun onFailure(errorCode: Int) {
                            finish(
                                ScreenCapture(
                                    bitmap = null,
                                    elapsedMillis = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - started,
                                    error = describeScreenshotError(errorCode)
                                )
                            )
                        }
                    }
                )
            } catch (t: Throwable) {
                finish(
                    ScreenCapture(
                        bitmap = null,
                        elapsedMillis = SystemClock.elapsedRealtime() - started,
                        error = "takeScreenshot failed: ${t::class.java.simpleName}: ${t.message}"
                    )
                )
            }
        }
    }

    private fun describeScreenshotError(errorCode: Int): String = when (errorCode) {
        AccessibilityService.ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_INTERVAL_TIME_SHORT ->
            "ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_INTERVAL_TIME_SHORT (system rate limit)"
        AccessibilityService.ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_INTERNAL_ERROR ->
            "ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_INTERNAL_ERROR"
        AccessibilityService.ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_NO_ACCESSIBILITY_ACCESS ->
            "ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_NO_ACCESSIBILITY_ACCESS"
        AccessibilityService.ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_INVALID_DISPLAY ->
            "ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT_INVALID_DISPLAY"
        else -> "ERROR_TAKE_SCREENSHOT code=$errorCode"
    }

    /** ML Kit's known Traditional Chinese misreads ([OcrCorrections]). */
    private val corrections: List<Pair<String, String>> by lazy { OcrCorrections.load(service) }

    private suspend fun recognize(bitmap: Bitmap): List<TextBox> {
        recognizerCreated = true
        val image = InputImage.fromBitmap(bitmap, 0)
        val text = withTimeoutOrNull(OCR_TIMEOUT_MILLIS) {
            suspendCancellableCoroutine<com.google.mlkit.vision.text.Text> { continuation ->
                recognizer.process(image)
                    .addOnSuccessListener { result -> continuation.resume(result) }
                    .addOnFailureListener { error -> continuation.resumeWith(Result.failure(error)) }
            }
        } ?: throw IllegalStateException("OCR timed out after ${OCR_TIMEOUT_MILLIS}ms")
        return text.textBlocks.flatMap { block ->
            block.lines.mapNotNull { line ->
                val rect = line.boundingBox ?: return@mapNotNull null
                val value = OcrCorrections.apply(line.text?.trim().orEmpty(), corrections)
                if (value.isEmpty()) return@mapNotNull null
                TextBox(value, Box(rect.left, rect.top, rect.right, rect.bottom), TextSource.OCR)
            }
        }
    }

    /** Walks the active window and turns visible labelled nodes into boxes. */
    private fun collectNodeBoxes(disabled: MutableList<Box>): List<TextBox> {
        val root = runCatching { service.rootInActiveWindow }.getOrNull() ?: return emptyList()
        val metrics = service.resources.displayMetrics
        val screenArea = metrics.widthPixels.toLong() * metrics.heightPixels
        val result = ArrayList<TextBox>(64)
        val seen = HashSet<String>()
        val queue = ArrayDeque<AccessibilityNodeInfo>()
        queue.addLast(root)
        var visited = 0
        val rect = Rect()

        while (queue.isNotEmpty() && visited < MAX_NODES) {
            val node = queue.removeFirst()
            visited++
            try {
                val visible = node.isVisibleToUser
                if (visible && !node.isEnabled && (node.isClickable || node.text != null)) {
                    node.getBoundsInScreen(rect)
                    if (rect.width() > 0 && rect.height() > 0 &&
                        rect.width().toLong() * rect.height() <= screenArea * MAX_NODE_AREA_RATIO
                    ) {
                        disabled.add(Box(rect.left, rect.top, rect.right, rect.bottom))
                    }
                }
                if (visible) {
                    val text = node.text?.toString()?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
                        ?: node.contentDescription?.toString()?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() }
                    if (!text.isNullOrEmpty()) {
                        node.getBoundsInScreen(rect)
                        val box = Box(rect.left, rect.top, rect.right, rect.bottom)
                        val area = box.area.toLong()
                        // Zero-size nodes are placeholders; near-full-screen
                        // nodes are containers whose text is already covered by
                        // their children, and their centre is not a tap target.
                        val usable = box.width > 0 && box.height > 0 &&
                            area <= screenArea * MAX_NODE_AREA_RATIO
                        if (usable && seen.add("$text|$box")) {
                            result.add(TextBox(text, box, TextSource.NODE))
                        }
                    }
                }
                for (index in 0 until node.childCount) {
                    runCatching { node.getChild(index) }.getOrNull()?.let { queue.addLast(it) }
                }
            } catch (t: Throwable) {
                // A window can disappear mid-walk; keep whatever was collected.
                continue
            }
        }
        return result
    }

    fun close() {
        if (recognizerCreated) runCatching { recognizer.close() }
        recognizerCreated = false
        if (screenshotPoolCreated) runCatching { screenshotPool.shutdownNow() }
        screenshotPoolCreated = false
    }

    companion object {
        /** Stops a hostile or enormous tree from taking seconds. */
        const val MAX_NODES = 1_500

        /** Containers covering most of the window are not text boxes. */
        const val MAX_NODE_AREA_RATIO = 0.9

        /** A screenshot callback must not hang a collection run. */
        const val SCREENSHOT_TIMEOUT_MILLIS = 5_000L

        /** ML Kit on a full screenshot is normally well under a second. */
        const val OCR_TIMEOUT_MILLIS = 15_000L
    }
}

/**
 * Spacing between accessibility screenshots. The platform rejects requests
 * closer than 333 ms (AccessibilityService.takeScreenshot); 350 ms leaves a
 * little room for clock jitter.
 */
object ScreenshotPacing {
    const val MIN_INTERVAL_MILLIS = 350L

    /** How long to wait before the next request; 0 when none was made yet. */
    fun waitMillis(lastAt: Long, now: Long): Long {
        if (lastAt < 0L) return 0L
        val since = now - lastAt
        return if (since >= MIN_INTERVAL_MILLIS || since < 0L) 0L else MIN_INTERVAL_MILLIS - since
    }
}

/** Which package a reading belongs to. */
object ForegroundResolver {
    /**
     * The active window's package when there is one, else the package the
     * accessibility events last reported. Events can miss a return to an app
     * that was already running; the window tree cannot.
     */
    fun packageName(rootPackage: String?, eventPackage: String?): String? =
        rootPackage?.trim()?.takeIf { it.isNotEmpty() } ?: eventPackage
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

/**
 * One rectangle on screen, in screenshot pixels.
 *
 * Integer pixel bounds (not float) because every source of truth here - the
 * accessibility node tree, ML Kit and the recorded pc-collector fixtures - is
 * integer, and a click needs an exact centre pixel.
 */
data class Box(val left: Int, val top: Int, val right: Int, val bottom: Int) {

    val width: Int get() = (right - left).coerceAtLeast(0)
    val height: Int get() = (bottom - top).coerceAtLeast(0)
    val area: Int get() = width * height
    val centerX: Int get() = (left + right) / 2
    val centerY: Int get() = (top + bottom) / 2

    fun containsPoint(x: Int, y: Int): Boolean = x in left until right && y in top until bottom

    fun union(other: Box): Box = Box(
        minOf(left, other.left),
        minOf(top, other.top),
        maxOf(right, other.right),
        maxOf(bottom, other.bottom)
    )

    fun contains(x: Int, y: Int): Boolean = x in left..right && y in top..bottom

    override fun toString(): String = "[$left,$top][$right,$bottom]"

    companion object {
        fun from(left: Int, top: Int, width: Int, height: Int): Box =
            Box(left, top, left + (width.coerceAtLeast(0)), top + (height.coerceAtLeast(0)))
    }
}

/**
 * Where a [TextBox] came from.
 *
 * The distinction matters downstream: a node box is authoritative for tapping
 * (it is the real view), while an OCR box only proves that pixels looked like
 * text. Phase 2 taps nodes whenever one exists.
 */
enum class TextSource { NODE, OCR }

/** A piece of text and the rectangle it occupies. */
data class TextBox(val text: String, val bounds: Box, val source: TextSource)

/** A match returned by [Snapshot.matches], ordered by confidence. */
data class TextBoxMatch(
    val text: String,
    val bounds: Box,
    val score: Int,
    val source: TextSource
) {
    val centerX: Int get() = bounds.centerX
    val centerY: Int get() = bounds.centerY
}

/**
 * Everything the collector knows about one moment on screen.
 *
 * The single model for both sources is deliberate (integration plan 禮3): the
 * 33 recorded `*.ocr.json` screens become JVM fixtures, so per-app rules can be
 * tested on a laptop before they ever touch a phone. [Source] on each box keeps
 * the provenance without a second parallel list.
 */
data class Snapshot(
    val width: Int,
    val height: Int,
    val capturedAt: Long,
    val foregroundPackage: String?,
    val foregroundActivity: String?,
    /** False on Android 10 and below, where `takeScreenshot` does not exist. */
    val ocrSupported: Boolean = true,
    val boxes: List<TextBox>,
    /** Wall time the OCR pass took, 0 when OCR did not run. */
    val ocrMillis: Long = 0L,
    /** Why OCR produced nothing, when it was expected to run. */
    val ocrError: String? = null,
    /**
     * Areas of nodes the app marks as not enabled (greyed-out buttons). A
     * reward label inside one is not tappable yet: AHEALTH's 140/160 ??
     * ?? were tapped twice each on 2026-11-16 at 124 minutes.
     */
    val disabled: List<Box> = emptyList()
) {

    val text: String get() = boxes.joinToString("\n") { it.text }

    fun boxesFrom(source: TextSource): List<TextBox> = boxes.filter { it.source == source }

    fun nodeCount(): Int = boxes.count { it.source == TextSource.NODE }

    fun ocrCount(): Int = boxes.count { it.source == TextSource.OCR }

    /**
     * Every box whose text matches [terms], best first - the port of
     * `OcrResult.matches`, including the `avoid` veto and the exact-only terms.
     * Duplicate matches on identical rectangles are collapsed, because the node
     * tree and OCR usually both see the same label.
     */
    fun matches(
        terms: Iterable<String>,
        avoid: Iterable<String> = emptyList(),
        exactTerms: Iterable<String> = emptyList(),
        minScore: Int = 1
    ): List<TextBoxMatch> {
        val avoided = avoid.map(::safeNormalize).filter { it.isNotEmpty() }
        val rewardNorms by lazy { terms.map(::safeNormalize).filter { it.isNotEmpty() } }
        val result = ArrayList<TextBoxMatch>()
        for (box in boxes) {
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(box.text)
            if (value.isEmpty()) continue
            if (avoided.any { it in value }) continue
            // OCR misreads one character now and then; a near-miss of an
            // avoid term is still avoided (node text is exact, no need).
            if (box.source == TextSource.OCR &&
                avoided.any { TextMatch.fuzzyAvoidHit(value, it, rewardNorms) }
            ) continue
            val score = TextMatch.bestTermsMatch(box.text, terms, emptyList(), exactTerms)
            if (score < minScore) continue
            result.add(TextBoxMatch(box.text, box.bounds, score, box.source))
        }
        result.sortWith(compareByDescending<TextBoxMatch> { it.score }.thenByDescending { it.bounds.area })
        val deduped = ArrayList<TextBoxMatch>(result.size)
        for (match in result) {
            if (deduped.any { it.bounds == match.bounds && it.text == match.text }) continue
            deduped.add(match)
        }
        return deduped
    }

    /** The single best match, or null. */
    fun find(
        terms: Iterable<String>,
        avoid: Iterable<String> = emptyList(),
        exactTerms: Iterable<String> = emptyList()
    ): TextBoxMatch? = matches(terms, avoid, exactTerms).firstOrNull()

    /** First box containing [text] after normalisation. */
    fun findLine(text: String, exact: Boolean = false): TextBox? {
        val wanted = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(text)
        if (wanted.isEmpty()) return null
        return boxes.firstOrNull {
            val value = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it.text)
            if (exact) value == wanted else wanted in value
        }
    }

    fun contains(text: String): Boolean {
        val wanted = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(text)
        return wanted.isNotEmpty() && boxes.any { wanted in TextMatch.normalizeLoose(it.text) }
    }

    private fun safeNormalize(value: String): String = TextMatch.normalizeLoose(value)
}

/**
 * Reads the format written by `reward_collector/ocr.py` (`parse_ocr_json`).
 *
 * Only line-level boxes are kept: pc-collector's per-word rectangles are useful
 * for tapping a keyword inside a long line, and that refinement can be ported
 * when phase 2 actually taps. Keeping the fixtures loadable now is what makes
 * them regression tests for the text rules.
 */
object OcrJson {

    fun parse(payload: String, capturedAt: Long = 0L): Snapshot {
        val root = MiniJson.parse(payload) as? Map<*, *>
            ?: throw IllegalArgumentException("OCR fixture is not a JSON object")
        val error = root["error"]?.toString()
        if (!error.isNullOrBlank()) throw IllegalArgumentException("OCR fixture reports error: $error")

        val width = intValue(root["width"])
        val height = intValue(root["height"])
        val rawLines = root["lines"] as? List<*> ?: emptyList<Any?>()
        val boxes = rawLines.mapNotNull { raw ->
            val line = raw as? Map<*, *> ?: return@mapNotNull null
            val text = line["text"]?.toString().orEmpty()
            val box = Box.from(
                left = intValue(line["x"]),
                top = intValue(line["y"]),
                width = intValue(line["w"]),
                height = intValue(line["h"])
            )
            TextBox(text = text, bounds = box, source = TextSource.OCR)
        }
        return Snapshot(
            width = width,
            height = height,
            capturedAt = capturedAt,
            foregroundPackage = null,
            foregroundActivity = null,
            boxes = boxes
        )
    }

    private fun intValue(value: Any?): Int = when (value) {
        is Long -> value.toInt()
        is Double -> value.toInt()
        is Number -> value.toInt()
        is String -> value.toIntOrNull() ?: 0
        else -> 0
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import android.content.Context
import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.graphics.BitmapFactory
import android.util.Log
import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.SupervisorJob
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.sync.Mutex
import kotlinx.coroutines.sync.withLock
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
import java.io.DataOutputStream
import java.io.File
import java.net.HttpURLConnection
import java.net.URL
import java.net.URLEncoder
import java.util.zip.ZipEntry
import java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream

/**
 * Where a run's record may go besides the phone: the user's own Telegram bot
 * (2026-11-13, requested by the user so failures can be read without a cable).
 *
 * The token and chat id are typed by the user on the phone and kept only in
 * the app's private preferences - never in the repo, never in a log line.
 */
object TelegramReportSettings {

    data class Config(val enabled: Boolean, val token: String, val chatId: String) {
        val usable: Boolean get() = enabled && token.isNotBlank() && chatId.isNotBlank()
    }

    private const val PREFS = "telegram_report"
    private const val KEY_ENABLED = "enabled"
    private const val KEY_TOKEN = "token"
    private const val KEY_CHAT = "chat_id"

    fun load(context: Context): Config {
        val prefs = context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
        return Config(
            enabled = prefs.getBoolean(KEY_ENABLED, false),
            token = prefs.getString(KEY_TOKEN, "").orEmpty(),
            chatId = prefs.getString(KEY_CHAT, "").orEmpty()
        )
    }

    fun save(context: Context, config: Config) {
        context.getSharedPreferences(PREFS, Context.MODE_PRIVATE).edit()
            .putBoolean(KEY_ENABLED, config.enabled)
            .putString(KEY_TOKEN, config.token.trim())
            .putString(KEY_CHAT, config.chatId.trim())
            .apply()
    }
}

/**
 * Records and screenshots are kept five days, then deleted (asked by the user
 * 2026-11-13). Applies to every run directory, the debug snapshots and the
 * zips made for sharing or Telegram.
 */
object RunRetention {

    const val KEEP_MILLIS = 5L * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000

    fun isExpired(lastModified: Long, now: Long, keepMillis: Long = KEEP_MILLIS): Boolean =
        lastModified > 0L && now - lastModified > keepMillis

    /** Deletes everything older than [KEEP_MILLIS]; returns how many entries went. */
    fun prune(context: Context, now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()): Int {
        var removed = 0
        val roots = listOf(
            File(context.filesDir, "collector_runs"),
            File(context.filesDir, "collector-snapshots"),
            File(context.cacheDir, "exports"),
            File(context.cacheDir, TelegramReporter.CACHE_DIR)
        )
        for (root in roots) {
            val entries = root.listFiles() ?: continue
            for (entry in entries) {
                if (!isExpired(newest(entry), now)) continue
                if (runCatching { entry.deleteRecursively() }.getOrDefault(false)) removed++
            }
        }
        return removed
    }

    /** A run directory counts from its newest file, not from when it was created. */
    private fun newest(entry: File): Long =
        if (entry.isDirectory) {
            entry.walkTopDown().filter { it.isFile }.maxOfOrNull { it.lastModified() } ?: entry.lastModified()
        } else {
            entry.lastModified()
        }
}

/**
 * Sends each finished run to Telegram as one zip and pins it.
 *
 * A bot never receives its own messages, so Claude cannot read what the app
 * sent through getUpdates; the pin makes the latest record reachable through
 * getChat. Sending happens after the run, off the run's thread, and a failure
 * (no network, bad token) leaves the run unsent so the next run retries it.
 * Collection itself never waits for Telegram.
 */
object TelegramReporter {

    const val CACHE_DIR = "telegram"
    const val SENT_MARK = ".sent_to_telegram"

    /** Older unsent runs beyond this are not sent (they are pruned within five days anyway). */
    const val MAX_PENDING = 5

    /** Screenshots per zip; the first and last ones tell most of a run. */
    const val MAX_SHOTS = 24
    private const val SHOT_WIDTH = 540
    private const val SHOT_QUALITY = 60

    /** Telegram's bot upload limit is 50 MB; stay far below it. */
    private const val MAX_ZIP_BYTES = 45L * 1024 * 1024

    private const val TAG = "TelegramReporter"
    private val scope = CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO)
    private val lock = Mutex()

    /** Called when a run ended: prune old records, then send what is unsent. */
    fun runFinished(context: Context) {
        val app = context.applicationContext
        scope.launch {
            lock.withLock {
                runCatching { RunRetention.prune(app) }
                runCatching { sendPending(app) }.onFailure { Log.w(TAG, "send failed: ${it.javaClass.simpleName}") }
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * A run that could not be sent is retried only for this long. Without it,
     * the dozens of runs recorded before the user turned Telegram on would be
     * sent five at a time after every later run (2026-11-13).
     */
    const val RETRY_WINDOW_MILLIS = 6L * 60 * 60 * 1000

    /** Runs that finished (have a summary) recently and were not sent yet, oldest first. */
    fun pendingRuns(
        runsRoot: File,
        limit: Int = MAX_PENDING,
        now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
    ): List<File> =
        (runsRoot.listFiles() ?: emptyArray())
            .filter { it.isDirectory && it.name.startsWith("run_") }
            .filter { !File(it, SENT_MARK).exists() }
            .filter {
                val summary = File(it, "summary.json")
                summary.isFile && now - summary.lastModified() <= RETRY_WINDOW_MILLIS
            }
            .sortedBy { it.name }
            .takeLast(limit)

    private fun sendPending(context: Context) {
        val config = TelegramReportSettings.load(context)
        if (!config.usable) return
        for (run in pendingRuns(File(context.filesDir, "collector_runs"))) {
            val zip = zipRun(context, run) ?: continue
            val messageId = sendDocument(config, zip, caption(run))
            runCatching { zip.delete() }
            if (messageId == null) return // network or token problem: retry after the next run
            runCatching { File(run, SENT_MARK).writeText(messageId.toString()) }
            pin(config, messageId)
        }
    }

    /** One line the user can read in the chat list. */
    fun caption(run: File): String {
        val summary = runCatching { File(run, "summary.json").readText() }.getOrDefault("")
        fun field(name: String): String =
            Regex("\"$name\"\\s*:\\s*\"?([^\",\\n}]*)").find(summary)?.groupValues?.get(1)?.trim().orEmpty()
        val manual = field("manual").ifEmpty { "0" }
        return "?撱??摰? ?芸??嗅?蝝??${field("name")}嚚???${field("endReason")}嚚? +
            "? ${field("rewards").ifEmpty { "0" }}嚚隤?${field("errors").ifEmpty { "0" }}嚚? +
            "??? $manual嚚?{run.name}嚚ommit ${field("commit")}"
    }

    /** console.log, events.jsonl and summary.json whole; screenshots shrunk to JPEG. */
    private fun zipRun(context: Context, run: File): File? {
        val dir = File(context.cacheDir, CACHE_DIR).apply { mkdirs() }
        val zip = File(dir, "${run.name}.zip")
        return runCatching {
            ZipOutputStream(zip.outputStream().buffered()).use { out ->
                for (name in listOf("summary.json", "console.log", "events.jsonl")) {
                    val file = File(run, name)
                    if (!file.isFile) continue
                    out.putNextEntry(ZipEntry("${run.name}/$name"))
                    file.inputStream().buffered().use { it.copyTo(out) }
                    out.closeEntry()
                }
                for (shot in pickShots(File(run, "shots").listFiles()?.toList().orEmpty())) {
                    val jpeg = shrink(shot) ?: continue
                    out.putNextEntry(ZipEntry("${run.name}/shots/${shot.nameWithoutExtension}.jpg"))
                    out.write(jpeg)
                    out.closeEntry()
                }
            }
            if (zip.length() > MAX_ZIP_BYTES) null else zip
        }.getOrNull()
    }

    /** The first and last screenshots when there are too many. */
    fun pickShots(shots: List<File>, max: Int = MAX_SHOTS): List<File> {
        val sorted = shots.filter { it.isFile }.sortedBy { it.name }
        if (sorted.size <= max) return sorted
        val half = max / 2
        return sorted.take(half) + sorted.takeLast(max - half)
    }

    private fun shrink(file: File): ByteArray? {
        val bitmap = BitmapFactory.decodeFile(file.absolutePath) ?: return null
        return try {
            val height = (bitmap.height * SHOT_WIDTH.toFloat() / bitmap.width).toInt().coerceAtLeast(1)
            val scaled = Bitmap.createScaledBitmap(bitmap, SHOT_WIDTH, height, true)
            ByteArrayOutputStream().use { bytes ->
                scaled.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, SHOT_QUALITY, bytes)
                if (scaled !== bitmap) scaled.recycle()
                bytes.toByteArray()
            }
        } finally {
            bitmap.recycle()
        }
    }

    /** A short message to check the settings; returns null on success, else why. */
    fun sendTest(config: TelegramReportSettings.Config): String? {
        if (config.token.isBlank() || config.chatId.isBlank()) return "隢‵ Bot Token ??Chat ID"
        val body = "chat_id=" + enc(config.chatId) + "&text=" + enc("?撱??摰?嚗elegram 蝝??葫閰行???)
        val (code, response) = post(config, "sendMessage", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", body.toByteArray())
        return if (code == 200 && response.contains("\"ok\":true")) null else describe(code, response)
    }

    private fun sendDocument(config: TelegramReportSettings.Config, file: File, caption: String): Long? {
        val boundary = "----rag${System.currentTimeMillis()}"
        val payload = ByteArrayOutputStream()
        DataOutputStream(payload).use { out ->
            fun part(name: String, value: String) {
                out.writeBytes("--$boundary\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"$name\"\r\n\r\n")
                out.write(value.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8))
                out.writeBytes("\r\n")
            }
            part("chat_id", config.chatId)
            part("caption", caption.take(1000))
            out.writeBytes(
                "--$boundary\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name=\"document\"; filename=\"${file.name}\"\r\n" +
                    "Content-Type: application/zip\r\n\r\n"
            )
            file.inputStream().use { it.copyTo(out) }
            out.writeBytes("\r\n--$boundary--\r\n")
        }
        val (code, response) = post(config, "sendDocument", "multipart/form-data; boundary=$boundary", payload.toByteArray())
        if (code != 200 || !response.contains("\"ok\":true")) {
            Log.w(TAG, "sendDocument failed: ${describe(code, response)}")
            return null
        }
        return Regex("\"message_id\"\\s*:\\s*(\\d+)").find(response)?.groupValues?.get(1)?.toLongOrNull()
    }

    private fun pin(config: TelegramReportSettings.Config, messageId: Long) {
        val body = "chat_id=" + enc(config.chatId) + "&message_id=$messageId&disable_notification=true"
        val (code, response) = post(config, "pinChatMessage", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", body.toByteArray())
        if (code != 200) Log.w(TAG, "pin failed: ${describe(code, response)}")
    }

    private fun post(
        config: TelegramReportSettings.Config,
        method: String,
        contentType: String,
        body: ByteArray
    ): Pair<Int, String> = runCatching {
        val connection = URL("https://api.telegram.org/bot${config.token}/$method").openConnection() as HttpURLConnection
        try {
            connection.requestMethod = "POST"
            connection.connectTimeout = 15_000
            connection.readTimeout = 60_000
            connection.doOutput = true
            connection.setRequestProperty("Content-Type", contentType)
            connection.outputStream.use { it.write(body) }
            val code = connection.responseCode
            val stream = if (code in 200..299) connection.inputStream else connection.errorStream
            code to (stream?.bufferedReader()?.use { it.readText() }.orEmpty())
        } finally {
            connection.disconnect()
        }
    }.getOrElse { -1 to (it.javaClass.simpleName) }

    /** Never includes the token: only the HTTP code and Telegram's description. */
    private fun describe(code: Int, response: String): String {
        val description = Regex("\"description\"\\s*:\\s*\"([^\"]*)\"").find(response)?.groupValues?.get(1)
        return if (code < 0) "???憭望?嚗?response嚗? else "HTTP $code ${description.orEmpty()}".trim()
    }

    private fun enc(value: String): String = URLEncoder.encode(value, "UTF-8")
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.collector

import java.text.Normalizer
import java.util.Locale

/**
 * Text comparison ported from pc-collector (`reward_collector/ui.py`).
 *
 * Why a port instead of a new matcher: the whole point of moving the collector
 * onto the phone is to reuse the keyword rules and the 33 recorded screens that
 * already proved them. Those rules were tuned against Windows OCR, which puts a
 * space between every CJK character ("????); removing *all* whitespace makes
 * the same rules work for the accessibility tree, ML Kit and the recorded
 * fixtures without three separate keyword tables.
 *
 * Pure Kotlin on purpose: every keyword decision is unit-tested on the JVM,
 * where the recorded fixtures live.
 */
object TextMatch {

    /**
     * Punctuation dropped by [normalizeLoose]. Same character set as the Python
     * implementation so a fixture that matched there also matches here.
     */
    private const val PUNCTUATION = "嚗?嚗?.!?:;()[]{}<>?"'?會/\\-_+"

    private val whitespace = Regex("\\s+")

    /**
     * NFKC + case folding + remove all whitespace.
     *
     * NFKC is what turns full-width Latin ("嚗∴慰嚗?) and full-width brackets into
     * their half-width forms, so an OCR pass and a node tree agree.
     */
    fun normalize(text: String): String {
        val folded = Normalizer.normalize(text, Normalizer.Form.NFKC).lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
        return whitespace.replace(folded, "")
    }

    /**
     * An OCR misread of an avoid term (2026-11-16: ML Kit read 蝳桃??as
     * ???/ 瞉抒??and the banner was tapped): some window of [label] differs
     * from [avoid] by exactly one character. Only for terms of 3+ characters,
     * and never where that window overlaps a reward term found in the label,
     * so 撌脤???does not veto the reward ?舫??? Inputs are normalized.
     */
    fun fuzzyAvoidHit(label: String, avoid: String, rewardTerms: Collection<String>): Boolean {
        val n = avoid.length
        if (n < FUZZY_MIN_LENGTH || label.length < n) return false
        if (avoid in label) return true
        val rewardSpans = ArrayList<IntRange>()
        for (term in rewardTerms) {
            if (term.isEmpty()) continue
            var at = label.indexOf(term)
            while (at >= 0) {
                rewardSpans += at until at + term.length
                at = label.indexOf(term, at + 1)
            }
        }
        for (start in 0..label.length - n) {
            var diff = 0
            var hanSwap = true
            for (i in 0 until n) {
                if (label[start + i] != avoid[i]) {
                    diff++
                    if (diff > 1) break
                    // A look-alike Han character (蝳?瞉???, not a digit or a
                    // letter: "0暺" is not a misread of ????
                    hanSwap = isHan(label[start + i]) && isHan(avoid[i])
                }
            }
            if (diff != 1 || !hanSwap) continue
            val window = start until start + n
            if (rewardSpans.none { it.first <= window.last && window.first <= it.last }) return true
        }
        return false
    }

    const val FUZZY_MIN_LENGTH = 3

    private fun isHan(ch: Char): Boolean = Character.UnicodeScript.of(ch.code) == Character.UnicodeScript.HAN

    /** [normalize] plus removal of decorative punctuation. */
    fun normalizeLoose(text: String): String {
        val value = normalize(text)
        if (value.isEmpty()) return value
        val builder = StringBuilder(value.length)
        for (ch in value) {
            if (PUNCTUATION.indexOf(ch) < 0) builder.append(ch)
        }
        return builder.toString()
    }

    /**
     * Best score of [terms] against [label], mirroring `best_terms_match`.
     *
     * 100 = the whole label is the term, 70 = the label starts with it, 50 = it
     * occurs somewhere. A term listed in [exactTerms] only counts as an exact
     * match, which is how short words such as "x" stop matching every label that
     * happens to contain that letter. Any [avoid] term anywhere in the label
     * vetoes the label entirely.
     */
    fun bestTermsMatch(
        label: String,
        terms: Iterable<String>,
        avoid: Iterable<String> = emptyList(),
        exactTerms: Iterable<String> = emptyList()
    ): Int {
        val value = normalizeLoose(label)
        if (value.isEmpty()) return 0
        for (term in avoid) {
            val normalized = normalizeLoose(term)
            if (normalized.isNotEmpty() && value.contains(normalized)) return 0
        }
        val exact = exactTerms.map(::normalizeLoose).filter { it.isNotEmpty() }.toSet()
        var score = 0
        for (term in terms) {
            val normalized = normalizeLoose(term)
            if (normalized.isEmpty()) continue
            when {
                value == normalized -> score = maxOf(score, 100)
                normalized in exact -> continue
                value.startsWith(normalized) -> score = maxOf(score, 70)
                value.contains(normalized) -> score = maxOf(score, 50)
            }
        }
        return score
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.controller

import android.os.Handler
import android.os.Looper
import com.rewardadguard.app.data.AppSettings
import com.rewardadguard.app.data.EventType
import com.rewardadguard.app.manager.EventLogger
import com.rewardadguard.app.session.SessionManager

/**
 * Brings the user back to the reward app after a blocked redirect
 * (spec sections 21-23).
 *
 * Order of attempts, cheapest and least intrusive first:
 *  1. `GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK` of the destination window.
 *  2. `performGlobalAction(GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK)` once more (single re-entrant ad
 *     chains).
 *  3. `GLOBAL_ACTION_RECENTS` is **never** used because it would steal focus.
 *
 * ### Why the scheduled path is asynchronous (ISS-01)
 *
 * The attempt used to run synchronously on the main looper and `Thread.sleep`
 * between the BACK press and the verification probe. Sleeping the main looper
 * freezes the accessibility service's own `onAccessibilityEvent`, so the
 * `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` that updates [foregroundPackageProvider] cannot be
 * delivered. The probe therefore read the *old* foreground package, the return
 * looked failed, and the guard pressed BACK again - pushing the already-returned
 * reward app away - while the looper stayed blocked for up to ~1.8s (ANR risk).
 *
 * [scheduleReturn] now releases the looper after each BACK and re-checks
 * [RETURN_SETTLE_MILLIS] later with `Handler.postDelayed`, so the service keeps
 * receiving events in between. The blocking [attemptReturn] is kept only for a
 * background/instrumentation caller that needs a result synchronously.
 *
 * The controller never launches the reward app itself unless the user enabled
 * AUTO_LAUNCH, keeping the "no aggressive app switching" promise.
 */
class ReturnController(
    private val logger: EventLogger,
    private val sessionManager: SessionManager,
    private val backAction: () -> Boolean,
    private val launchSourceAction: (String) -> Boolean
) {

    /** Result of a return attempt, so callers can log and update the session. */
    data class ReturnResult(
        val success: Boolean,
        val method: String,
        val attempts: Int
    )

    private val handler = Handler(Looper.getMainLooper())

    /** The next runnable of the in-flight async chain, so it can be cancelled. */
    private var pendingRunnable: Runnable? = null

    @Volatile
    private var returnInProgress: Boolean = false

    /**
     * Verification hook. The accessibility service overrides this through
     * [foregroundPackageProvider]; returning true means the reward app is back.
     */
    var foregroundPackageProvider: (() -> String?)? = null

    /**
     * Schedules a return attempt on the main looper.
     *
     * Returns immediately: the BACK press and the verification probe run as two
     * separate, non-blocking steps so the looper (and therefore
     * `onAccessibilityEvent`) stays responsive in between.
     *
     * @param destinationPackage the app that must be left
     * @param sourcePackage the reward app to come back to
     * @param onComplete invoked on the main looper with the final result
     */
    fun scheduleReturn(
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        settings: AppSettings,
        delayMillis: Long = 0L,
        onComplete: ((ReturnResult) -> Unit)? = null
    ) {
        if (!settings.autoReturnEnabled) {
            logger.log(
                eventType = EventType.RETURN,
                sessionId = sessionManager.currentSessionId ?: EventLogger.NO_SESSION,
                sourcePackage = sourcePackage,
                destinationPackage = destinationPackage,
                detectionMethod = "RETURN_DISABLED",
                action = "RETURN_SKIPPED",
                result = "SKIPPED",
                message = "auto return disabled by user"
            )
            return
        }
        cancelPending()
        val start = Runnable {
            stepReturnAsync(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, settings, attempt = 1, onComplete = onComplete)
        }
        pendingRunnable = start
        handler.postDelayed(start, delayMillis.coerceAtLeast(0L))
    }

    /** One BACK press, then a deferred verification step. Never blocks. */
    private fun stepReturnAsync(
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        settings: AppSettings,
        attempt: Int,
        onComplete: ((ReturnResult) -> Unit)?
    ) {
        // The reward app may already be back: the 120 ms delay between
        // scheduling and this step (and the settle time after a previous BACK)
        // is enough for the ad to close on its own. Pressing BACK here lands on
        // the reward app's main screen and closes it (field report 2026-10-30).
        if (isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)) {
            finishReturn(true, "ALREADY_IN_SOURCE", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            return
        }
        // A BACK is only safe while the recorded redirect destination is the app
        // in front. If the user switched to another app - or the foreground
        // cannot be resolved - pressing BACK would close that app, which is the
        // field bug where ordinary apps were force-closed by the guard.
        if (!isDestinationForeground(destinationPackage)) {
            abortReturn(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, attempt, onComplete)
            return
        }
        returnInProgress = true
        val dispatched = runCatching { backAction() }.getOrDefault(false)
        if (!dispatched) {
            finishReturn(false, "BACK_NOT_DISPATCHED", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            return
        }
        if (!settings.verifyReturn) {
            finishReturn(true, "GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            return
        }
        // Hand the looper back before probing. During the wait the accessibility
        // service receives the real window transition and updates the probe.
        scheduleVerify(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, settings, attempt, onComplete)
    }

    /**
     * Probes the foreground up to [RETURN_VERIFY_POLLS] times before deciding a
     * BACK did not work.
     *
     * A cold-starting destination (Shopee takes ~2 s on the field device) is not
     * in front after a single [RETURN_SETTLE_MILLIS] probe, so the old code
     * pressed BACK again - on the wrong screen - and then reported a failure
     * (field report 2026-10-30, root cause 3).
     */
    private fun scheduleVerify(
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        settings: AppSettings,
        attempt: Int,
        onComplete: ((ReturnResult) -> Unit)?,
        pollsLeft: Int = RETURN_VERIFY_POLLS
    ) {
        val verify = Runnable {
            if (isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)) {
                finishReturn(true, "GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            } else if (pollsLeft > 1) {
                scheduleVerify(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, settings, attempt, onComplete, pollsLeft - 1)
            } else if (attempt < settings.maxReturnAttempts) {
                stepReturnAsync(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, settings, attempt + 1, onComplete)
            } else if (settings.autoLaunchRewardApp) {
                relaunchAndVerify(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, attempt, onComplete)
            } else {
                finishReturn(false, "GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            }
        }
        pendingRunnable = verify
        handler.postDelayed(verify, RETURN_SETTLE_MILLIS)
    }

    /** Launches the reward app, then verifies it one settle interval later. */
    private fun relaunchAndVerify(
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        attempt: Int,
        onComplete: ((ReturnResult) -> Unit)?,
        pollsLeft: Int = RETURN_VERIFY_POLLS
    ) {
        // Never relaunch an app that is already in front: that would restart its
        // main activity for no reason (field report 2026-10-30).
        if (isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)) {
            finishReturn(true, "ALREADY_IN_SOURCE", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            return
        }
        // The user moved on to another app, or the foreground is unknown: do not
        // pull the reward app over it.
        val foreground = foregroundPackageProvider?.invoke()
        if (foreground.isNullOrBlank() ||
            (foreground != sourcePackage && foreground != destinationPackage)
        ) {
            abortReturn(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, attempt, onComplete)
            return
        }
        val launched = runCatching { launchSourceAction(sourcePackage) }.getOrDefault(false)
        if (!launched) {
            finishReturn(false, "AUTO_LAUNCH_FAILED", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            return
        }
        scheduleLaunchVerify(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, attempt, onComplete, pollsLeft)
    }

    private fun scheduleLaunchVerify(
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        attempt: Int,
        onComplete: ((ReturnResult) -> Unit)?,
        pollsLeft: Int
    ) {
        val verify = Runnable {
            // Without a probe (unit tests) a successful launch is trusted.
            val ok = foregroundPackageProvider == null || isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)
            if (ok) {
                finishReturn(true, "AUTO_LAUNCH_REWARD_APP", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            } else if (pollsLeft > 1) {
                scheduleLaunchVerify(destinationPackage, sourcePackage, attempt, onComplete, pollsLeft - 1)
            } else {
                finishReturn(false, "AUTO_LAUNCH_REWARD_APP", attempt, destinationPackage, sourcePackage, onComplete)
            }
        }
        pendingRunnable = verify
        handler.postDelayed(verify, RETURN_SETTLE_MILLIS)
    }

    /** Logs the outcome once, then reports it to the optional completion callback. */
    private fun finishReturn(
        success: Boolean,
        method: String,
        attempts: Int,
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        onComplete: ((ReturnResult) -> Unit)?
    ) {
        pendingRunnable = null
        returnInProgress = false
        logger.log(
            eventType = if (success) EventType.RETURN else EventType.RETURN_FAILED,
            sessionId = sessionManager.currentSessionId ?: EventLogger.NO_SESSION,
            sourcePackage = sourcePackage,
            destinationPackage = destinationPackage,
            detectionMethod = method,
            action = "RETURN_ATTEMPT",
            result = if (success) "SUCCESS" else "FAILED",
            message = "attempts=$attempts"
        )
        onComplete?.invoke(ReturnResult(success, method, attempts))
    }

    /**
     * Stops a return chain because the app in front is no longer the redirect
     * destination (the user switched apps, or the foreground is unknown).
     *
     * No BACK is pressed and the reward app is not relaunched: both would act on
     * an app the guard was never allowed to touch.
     */
    private fun abortReturn(
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        attempt: Int,
        onComplete: ((ReturnResult) -> Unit)?
    ) {
        pendingRunnable = null
        returnInProgress = false
        val foreground = foregroundPackageProvider?.invoke()
        val method = if (foreground.isNullOrBlank()) "FOREGROUND_UNKNOWN" else "FOREGROUND_CHANGED"
        logger.log(
            eventType = EventType.RETURN,
            sessionId = sessionManager.currentSessionId ?: EventLogger.NO_SESSION,
            sourcePackage = sourcePackage,
            destinationPackage = destinationPackage,
            detectionMethod = method,
            action = "RETURN_SKIPPED",
            result = "SKIPPED",
            message = "foreground=$foreground attempt=$attempt"
        )
        onComplete?.invoke(ReturnResult(false, method, attempt))
    }

    /**
     * Blocking variant, kept for a background/instrumentation caller that wants
     * the result synchronously. Production uses [scheduleReturn]; do **not** call
     * this from the main looper, because it sleeps between attempts.
     *
     * @param destinationPackage the app that must be left
     * @param sourcePackage the reward app to come back to
     */
    fun attemptReturn(
        destinationPackage: String,
        sourcePackage: String,
        settings: AppSettings
    ): ReturnResult {
        if (returnInProgress) {
            return ReturnResult(false, "ALREADY_IN_PROGRESS", 0)
        }
        returnInProgress = true
        var attempts = 0
        var success = false
        var method = "NONE"

        try {
            // Attempt 1..maxAttempts: BACK presses.
            while (attempts < settings.maxReturnAttempts && !success) {
                // Already back: a BACK here would close the reward app.
                if (isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)) {
                    method = "ALREADY_IN_SOURCE"
                    success = true
                    break
                }
                // Never press BACK in an app that is not the redirect destination.
                if (!isDestinationForeground(destinationPackage)) {
                    method = if (foregroundPackageProvider?.invoke().isNullOrBlank()) {
                        "FOREGROUND_UNKNOWN"
                    } else {
                        "FOREGROUND_CHANGED"
                    }
                    break
                }
                attempts++
                val dispatched = runCatching { backAction() }.getOrDefault(false)
                if (!dispatched) {
                    method = "BACK_NOT_DISPATCHED"
                    break
                }
                method = "GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK"
                if (!settings.verifyReturn) {
                    // Verification disabled: trust the dispatch but still log it.
                    success = true
                    break
                }
                // Give the window manager time to settle before the next probe.
                Thread.sleep(RETURN_SETTLE_MILLIS)
                if (isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)) {
                    success = true
                }
            }

            if (!success && settings.autoLaunchRewardApp && attempts >= settings.maxReturnAttempts) {
                val foreground = foregroundPackageProvider?.invoke()
                if (isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)) {
                    method = "ALREADY_IN_SOURCE"
                    success = true
                } else if (foreground.isNullOrBlank() ||
                    (foreground != sourcePackage && foreground != destinationPackage)
                ) {
                    // The user is elsewhere: never pull the reward app over it.
                    method = if (foreground.isNullOrBlank()) "FOREGROUND_UNKNOWN" else "FOREGROUND_CHANGED"
                } else {
                    val launched = runCatching { launchSourceAction(sourcePackage) }.getOrDefault(false)
                    if (launched) {
                        method = "AUTO_LAUNCH_REWARD_APP"
                        Thread.sleep(RETURN_SETTLE_MILLIS)
                        // Verify the launch instead of trusting it. The previous
                        // `isSourceForeground(sourcePackage) || true` reported success
                        // unconditionally, so a launch that never reached the
                        // foreground was still logged as a RETURN (root cause 4.4).
                        success = foregroundPackageProvider == null || isSourceForeground(sourcePackage)
                    }
                }
            }
        } catch (t: Throwable) {
            logger.log(
                eventType = EventType.ERROR,
                sessionId = sessionManager.currentSessionId ?: EventLogger.NO_SESSION,
                sourcePackage = sourcePackage,
                destinationPackage = destinationPackage,
                detectionMethod = "ReturnController",
                action = "RETURN_ERROR",
                result = "FAILED",
                message = "return failed",
                error = t.message
            )
        } finally {
            returnInProgress = false
        }

        logger.log(
            eventType = if (success) EventType.RETURN else EventType.RETURN_FAILED,
            sessionId = sessionManager.currentSessionId ?: EventLogger.NO_SESSION,
            sourcePackage = sourcePackage,
            destinationPackage = destinationPackage,
            detectionMethod = method,
            action = "RETURN_ATTEMPT",
            result = if (success) "SUCCESS" else "FAILED",
            message = "attempts=$attempts"
        )
        return ReturnResult(success, method, attempts)
    }

    private fun isSourceForeground(sourcePackage: String): Boolean =
        foregroundPackageProvider?.invoke() == sourcePackage

    /** True only when the recorded redirect destination is really in front. */
    private fun isDestinationForeground(destinationPackage: String): Boolean =
        foregroundPackageProvider?.invoke() == destinationPackage

    fun cancelPending() {
        pendingRunnable?.let { handler.removeCallbacks(it) }
        pendingRunnable = null
        returnInProgress = false
    }

    val isReturnInProgress: Boolean get() = returnInProgress

    /**
     * True while a return is scheduled or running, including the delay before
     * its first step (when [isReturnInProgress] is still false).
     */
    val hasPendingReturn: Boolean get() = pendingRunnable != null || returnInProgress

    companion object {
        /** Time given to the window manager between a BACK press and a probe. */
        const val RETURN_SETTLE_MILLIS = 450L

        /**
         * How many probes one BACK gets before it is considered failed.
         *
         * Polling (instead of one 450 ms probe) covers slow cold starts such as
         * Shopee (~2 s on the field device) without pressing BACK a second time
         * on the wrong screen (field report 2026-10-30). Five probes give the
         * destination ~2.25 s to settle.
         */
        const val RETURN_VERIFY_POLLS = 5
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.data

/** Protection level, spec section 8. */
enum class ProtectionMode {
    OFF,
    LOG_ONLY,
    BLOCK;

    companion object {
        fun fromName(name: String?): ProtectionMode =
            entries.firstOrNull { it.name == name } ?: BLOCK
    }
}

/** What the guard is allowed to do with a suspicious redirect (spec section 20). */
enum class RedirectPolicy {
    LOG_ONLY,
    BLOCK_IMMEDIATELY,
    BLOCK_AFTER_GRACE;

    companion object {
        fun fromName(name: String?): RedirectPolicy =
            entries.firstOrNull { it.name == name } ?: BLOCK_AFTER_GRACE
    }
}

/** What the close-button guard is allowed to do (spec section 24-27). */
enum class AssistAction {
    /** Only detect and log the X, never click. */
    NONE,

    /** Highlight/log the X and click it through the accessibility node. */
    ASSIST_CLICK,

    /**
     * Same as [ASSIST_CLICK] but only after the user has been idle, so
     * user-initiated closes always win.
     */
    ASSIST_WHEN_IDLE,

    /** Re-read the tree and click the X as soon as it appears (most aggressive). */
    ASSIST_TIMED_RETRY;

    companion object {
        fun fromName(name: String?): AssistAction =
            entries.firstOrNull { it.name == name } ?: ASSIST_WHEN_IDLE
    }
}

/**
 * Immutable snapshot of all user settings. Held in memory by the accessibility
 * service and refreshed by a DataStore flow, so hot paths never touch disk.
 */
data class AppSettings(
    val protectionMode: ProtectionMode = ProtectionMode.BLOCK,
    val externalRedirectProtection: Boolean = true,
    val closeButtonAssistance: Boolean = true,
    /** Assisted close control, see [AssistAction]. */
    val assistAction: AssistAction = AssistAction.ASSIST_CLICK,
    val xClickAreaMultiplier: Int = 3,
    val smartRedirectEnabled: Boolean = true,
    /**
     * Block immediately on the first suspicious jump instead of using the grace
     * period.
     *
     * Default is BLOCK_IMMEDIATELY. Field data (2026-10-09, a real rewarded ad):
     * with BLOCK_AFTER_GRACE, a short (<1s) store/external hop never outlived the
     * 700ms grace, so 9 redirects produced 0 blocks. BLOCK_IMMEDIATELY blocked 8
     * of the same 9 and returned the user each time. The first low-risk hop after
     * a real tap is still only observed (see SmartRedirectEngine, spec test 55),
     * so legitimate CTA flows keep working.
     */
    val redirectPolicy: RedirectPolicy = RedirectPolicy.BLOCK_IMMEDIATELY,
    /** Milliseconds the destination must stay in the foreground before blocking. */
    val blockGraceMillis: Long = 700L,
    /** Log only for apps that were not explicitly promoted to BLOCK. */
    val newAppSafeModeEnabled: Boolean = true,
    val loggingEnabled: Boolean = true,
    val maxLogEvents: Int = 10_000,
    val maxSessions: Int = 500,
    /** Send a single low-priority notification when the service connects. */
    val statusNotificationEnabled: Boolean = true,
    /** Test mode: simulate reward app -> external app transitions. */
    val testModeEnabled: Boolean = false,
    /** Return to the reward app after a blocked redirect. */
    val autoReturnEnabled: Boolean = true,
    /**
     * Launch the reward app if Back presses were not enough.
     *
     * On by default: against a destination that swallows Back (the Play Store
     * opened from an ad CTA was measured to ignore two Back presses), a guard
     * that only presses Back leaves the user stranded in the external app. The
     * relaunch is the fallback that actually returns them.
     */
    val autoLaunchRewardApp: Boolean = true,
    /** Verify that the reward app really came back, instead of trusting dispatch. */
    val verifyReturn: Boolean = true,
    /** Maximum number of Back presses per return attempt (1..3). */
    val maxReturnAttempts: Int = 2,
    /**
     * Guarding is paused until this wall-clock time; 0 = running, and
     * [PAUSED_INDEFINITELY] = stopped until the user resumes it.
     *
     * A pause keeps the accessibility service enabled - re-enabling it on
     * HyperOS needs a confirmation dialog with a countdown and sometimes the
     * "restricted settings" detour - but makes the service subscribe to no
     * events at all, so a paused guard costs the phone nothing (2026-11-04).
     */
    val pausedUntil: Long = 0L
) {
    /** True while guarding is paused or stopped at [now]. */
    fun isPaused(now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()): Boolean = pausedUntil > now

    /** True when the pause has no end time (stopped). */
    val isStopped: Boolean
        get() = pausedUntil == PAUSED_INDEFINITELY

    val xClickAreaScale: Float
        get() = xClickAreaMultiplier.coerceIn(1, 5).toFloat()

    /** True when redirect protection may interrupt the user right now. */
    val canBlock: Boolean
        get() = protectionMode == ProtectionMode.BLOCK && externalRedirectProtection

    /** True when the guard must stay observational. */
    val isLogOnly: Boolean
        get() = protectionMode == ProtectionMode.LOG_ONLY

    val protectionEnabled: Boolean
        get() = protectionMode != ProtectionMode.OFF

    companion object {
        /** [pausedUntil] value meaning "stopped until resumed by hand". */
        const val PAUSED_INDEFINITELY = Long.MAX_VALUE
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.data

/**
 * Log category. Mirrors the categories required by the spec (section 30).
 * Stored as a plain string in Room for forward compatibility.
 */
enum class EventCategory {
    APP,
    SESSION,
    AD,
    CLOSE,
    JUMP,
    BLOCK,
    RETURN,
    ERROR,
    EXTRA, 
    SYSTEM;

    companion object {
        fun fromName(name: String?): EventCategory =
            entries.firstOrNull { it.name.equals(name, ignoreCase = true) } ?: SYSTEM
    }
}

/**
 * Machine readable event type. Kept as an enum so that both the logger and the
 * tests share one single source of truth.
 */
enum class EventType {
    SESSION_START,
    SESSION_STATE,
    SESSION_END,
    SESSION_SUMMARY,
    APP_CHANGE,
    POSSIBLE_AD_SESSION,
    AD_SESSION_ACTIVE,
    AD_SESSION_END,
    POSSIBLE_REDIRECT,
    REDIRECT_DETECTED,
    REDIRECT_RISK,
    EXTERNAL_APP,
    BROWSER,
    STORE,
    DEEP_LINK,
    GAME,
    RETURNED_TO_SOURCE,
    BLOCK,
    BLOCK_SKIPPED,
    RETURN,
    RETURN_DECISION,
    RETURN_FAILED,
    CLOSE_DETECT,
    CLOSE_BOUNDS,
    CLOSE_RESULT,
    CLOSE_ACTION,
    CLOSE_MISS,
    /**
     * A close button was found but deliberately not acted on; the message names
     * the reason ([com.rewardadguard.app.guard.AssistDecision]).
     *
     * Distinct from [CLOSE_MISS], which now means only "no usable match". The two
     * were previously merged, which made a working guard look broken.
     */
    CLOSE_DECISION,
    /**
     * An automatic action on the ad page itself: clicking the literal
     * `[close]` label or the `[>>]` / `[->]` next-step label of a monitored
     * reward app's ad.
     */
    AD_ACTION,
    ERROR,
    SERVICE_CONNECTED,
    SERVICE_DISCONNECTED,
    SERVICE_INTERRUPTED,
    SETTINGS_CHANGED,
    TEST_REDIRECT_SIMULATED,
    /** Informational entry that explains why the guard stayed passive. */
    EXTRA_INFO,
    LOG_CLEARED,
    LOG_EXPORTED,

    /**
     * An action or decision of the automatic reward collector (`collector`
     * package). Kept separate from the guard's event types so a log export makes
     * it obvious which side of the integration did something.
     */
    COLLECTOR;

    fun category(): EventCategory = when (this) {
        SESSION_START, SESSION_STATE, SESSION_END, SESSION_SUMMARY -> EventCategory.SESSION
        APP_CHANGE -> EventCategory.APP
        POSSIBLE_AD_SESSION, AD_SESSION_ACTIVE, AD_SESSION_END, AD_ACTION -> EventCategory.AD
        CLOSE_DETECT, CLOSE_BOUNDS, CLOSE_RESULT, CLOSE_ACTION, CLOSE_MISS,
        CLOSE_DECISION -> EventCategory.CLOSE
        POSSIBLE_REDIRECT, REDIRECT_DETECTED, REDIRECT_RISK, EXTERNAL_APP, BROWSER, STORE,
        DEEP_LINK, GAME, RETURNED_TO_SOURCE -> EventCategory.JUMP
        BLOCK, BLOCK_SKIPPED -> EventCategory.BLOCK
        RETURN, RETURN_DECISION, RETURN_FAILED -> EventCategory.RETURN
        ERROR -> EventCategory.ERROR
        EXTRA_INFO, COLLECTOR -> EventCategory.EXTRA
        SERVICE_CONNECTED, SERVICE_DISCONNECTED, SERVICE_INTERRUPTED, SETTINGS_CHANGED,
        TEST_REDIRECT_SIMULATED, LOG_CLEARED, LOG_EXPORTED -> EventCategory.SYSTEM
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.data

import androidx.room.Entity
import androidx.room.PrimaryKey

/**
 * One persisted log line.
 *
 * Privacy: only package names, event metadata and timestamps are stored.
 * UI text of third party apps is never persisted (see spec section 50).
 */
@Entity(tableName = "events")
data class EventRecord(
    @PrimaryKey(autoGenerate = true)
    val id: Long = 0L,
    val timestamp: Long,
    val sessionId: String,
    val eventType: String,
    val category: String,
    val sourcePackage: String?,
    val destinationPackage: String?,
    val detectionMethod: String?,
    val action: String?,
    val result: String?,
    val message: String?,
    val error: String?
)
