package com.rewardadguard.app.data

import androidx.room.Dao
import androidx.room.Insert
import androidx.room.OnConflictStrategy
import androidx.room.Query
import androidx.room.Update

@Dao
interface EventDao {

    @Insert
    suspend fun insert(event: EventRecord): Long

    @Query("SELECT * FROM events ORDER BY timestamp DESC, id DESC LIMIT :limit")
    suspend fun recent(limit: Int): List<EventRecord>

    @Query(
        """
        SELECT * FROM events
        WHERE category = :category
        ORDER BY timestamp DESC, id DESC LIMIT :limit
        """
    )
    suspend fun recentByCategory(category: String, limit: Int): List<EventRecord>

    @Query(
        """
        SELECT * FROM events
        WHERE (:sessionId IS NULL OR sessionId LIKE '%' || :sessionId || '%')
          AND (:packageName IS NULL OR sourcePackage LIKE '%' || :packageName || '%'
               OR destinationPackage LIKE '%' || :packageName || '%')
          AND (:eventType IS NULL OR eventType LIKE '%' || :eventType || '%')
          AND (:from IS NULL OR timestamp >= :from)
          AND (:to IS NULL OR timestamp <= :to)
        ORDER BY timestamp DESC, id DESC LIMIT :limit
        """
    )
    suspend fun search(
        sessionId: String?,
        packageName: String?,
        eventType: String?,
        from: Long?,
        to: Long?,
        limit: Int
    ): List<EventRecord>

    @Query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events")
    suspend fun count(): Int

    /**
     * FIFO trim: keep the newest [keep] rows, delete everything older.
     * Called after inserts so the log can never grow without bound.
     */
    @Query(
        """
        DELETE FROM events WHERE id NOT IN (
            SELECT id FROM events ORDER BY timestamp DESC, id DESC LIMIT :keep
        )
        """
    )
    suspend fun trimToNewest(keep: Int): Int

    @Query("DELETE FROM events")
    suspend fun deleteAll()

    /** Statistics primitives. */
    @Query(
        """
        SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events
        WHERE eventType = :eventType AND timestamp >= :since
        """
    )
    suspend fun countByTypeSince(eventType: String, since: Long): Int

    @Query(
        """
        SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events
        WHERE category = :category AND timestamp >= :since
        """
    )
    suspend fun countByCategorySince(category: String, since: Long): Int

    @Query(
        """
        SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events
        WHERE eventType = :eventType AND timestamp >= :since
          AND (sourcePackage = :packageName OR destinationPackage = :packageName)
        """
    )
    suspend fun countByTypeForPackage(eventType: String, packageName: String, since: Long): Int

    @Query(
        """
        SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events
        WHERE eventType = 'SESSION_START'
          AND sourcePackage = :packageName
          AND timestamp >= :since
        """
    )
    suspend fun countSessionsSince(packageName: String, since: Long): Int

    /** Distinct source packages seen at least once (used for per-app aggregation). */
    @Query("SELECT DISTINCT sourcePackage FROM events WHERE eventType = 'SESSION_START'")
    suspend fun distinctSessionSources(): List<String>
}

@Dao
interface SessionDao {

    @Insert(onConflict = OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE)
    suspend fun upsert(session: SessionRecord)

    @Update
    suspend fun update(session: SessionRecord)

    @Query("SELECT * FROM sessions ORDER BY startedAt DESC LIMIT :limit")
    suspend fun recent(limit: Int): List<SessionRecord>

    @Query("SELECT * FROM sessions WHERE sessionId = :sessionId")
    suspend fun byId(sessionId: String): SessionRecord?

    @Query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sessions WHERE startedAt >= :since")
    suspend fun countSince(since: Long): Int

    @Query("DELETE FROM sessions")
    suspend fun deleteAll()

    /** Keep only the newest [keep] sessions (FIFO), returns rows removed. */
    @Query(
        """
        DELETE FROM sessions WHERE sessionId NOT IN (
            SELECT sessionId FROM sessions ORDER BY startedAt DESC LIMIT :keep
        )
        """
    )
    suspend fun trimToNewest(keep: Int): Int
}

@Dao
interface AppStatsDao {

    @Insert(onConflict = OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE)
    suspend fun upsert(stats: AppStatsRecord)

    @Query("SELECT * FROM app_stats ORDER BY packageName ASC")
    suspend fun all(): List<AppStatsRecord>

    @Query("SELECT * FROM app_stats WHERE packageName = :packageName")
    suspend fun byPackage(packageName: String): AppStatsRecord?

    @Query("DELETE FROM app_stats")
    suspend fun deleteAll()
}

    abstract fun sessionDao(): SessionDao

                    context.applicationContext,

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\detector\AdActionDetector.kt
==============================================================================
package com.rewardadguard.app.detector

/**
 * The two literal controls an ad page is allowed to expose to the guard.
 *
 * Deliberately an exhaustive list: only text rendered exactly as `[close]` or
 * `[>>]` is recognised, so ordinary words such as "Close", the ad's "Google
 * Play >>" call to action, or an article that merely mentions a close button
 * can never be mistaken for one of these controls.
 */
enum class AdActionKind {
    /** `[close]`: dismiss the ad and go back to the reward collection flow. */
    CLOSE,

    /** `[>>]`: advance the ad to its next step. */
    NEXT
}

/**
 * One matched `[close]` / `[>>]` control.
 *
 * [node] is the snapshot of the *labelled* node. Whether it is actually
 * operable is decided against the live tree at click time, because a labelled
 * `TextView` is often wrapped in the clickable button that really receives the
 * tap.
 */
data class AdActionMatch(
    val kind: AdActionKind,
    val node: NodeSnapshot,
    val method: String,
    /** The exact label that matched, e.g. `[>>]` or `[->]`. */
    val token: String = AdActionDetector.tokenOf(kind)
) {
    /** `72x72`, for the log. */
    fun boundsLabel(): String = "${node.width}x${node.height}"

    /** Stable id linking DISPATCHED and VERIFIED rows of one action. */
    fun correlationId(): String =
        "cid=${node.left},${node.top},${node.right},${node.bottom}#$token"
}

/**
 * Detects the literal `[close]` and `[>>]` ad-page controls.
 *
 * Pure Kotlin over [NodeSnapshot], so the matching rules are unit tested on the
 * JVM. The service is responsible for the two things this object cannot know:
 *  - the node is inside a window of a *monitored reward app* (the caller checks
 *    the window's package before calling in),
 *  - a real clickable target exists on top of the label.
 */
object AdActionDetector {

    /** The exact close label, compared case-insensitively after normalisation. */
    const val CLOSE_TOKEN = "[close]"

    /** The exact next-step label. */
    const val NEXT_TOKEN = "[>>]"

    /** The alternate next-step label. */
    const val NEXT_ARROW_TOKEN = "[->]"

    /** Full-width bracket variants that some ad renderers emit. */
    private const val CLOSE_TOKEN_WIDE = "\uFF3Bclose\uFF3D"
    private const val NEXT_TOKEN_WIDE = "\uFF3B>>\uFF3D"
    private const val NEXT_ARROW_TOKEN_WIDE = "\uFF3B->\uFF3D"

    /** The label string of [kind], for logging. */
    fun tokenOf(kind: AdActionKind): String = when (kind) {
        AdActionKind.CLOSE -> CLOSE_TOKEN
        AdActionKind.NEXT -> NEXT_TOKEN
    }

    /**
     * Maps a node label to a [AdActionKind].
     *
     * The whole label must be the token: `[close] (3s)` or "Tap [close]" is
     * intentionally *not* matched, because a partial match is how a normal app's
     * UI text gets mistaken for an ad control.
     */
    fun classify(label: String?): AdActionKind? =
        if (matchedToken(label) != null) {
            when (normalize(label)) {
                CLOSE_TOKEN, CLOSE_TOKEN_WIDE -> AdActionKind.CLOSE
                else -> AdActionKind.NEXT
            }
        } else {
            null
        }

    /** The next-step label [node] shows, or null when it shows none. */
    internal fun tokenOf(node: NodeSnapshot): String? =
        matchedToken(node.text) ?: matchedToken(node.contentDescription)

    /** The exact token [label] spells, or null when it is not a control label. */
    fun matchedToken(label: String?): String? = when (normalize(label)) {
        CLOSE_TOKEN, CLOSE_TOKEN_WIDE -> CLOSE_TOKEN
        NEXT_TOKEN, NEXT_TOKEN_WIDE -> NEXT_TOKEN
        NEXT_ARROW_TOKEN, NEXT_ARROW_TOKEN_WIDE -> NEXT_ARROW_TOKEN
        else -> null
    }

    /**
     * True when [node] shows the label of [kind] and can plausibly be a control.
     *
     * Visibility, non-zero bounds and a size sanity check are enforced here; the
     * clickable-target check happens against the live tree in the service.
     */
    fun isLabelled(node: NodeSnapshot, kind: AdActionKind): Boolean {
        if (!node.visible) return false
        if (node.width <= 0 || node.height <= 0) return false
        return classify(tokenOf(node)) == kind
    }

    /**
     * Picks the control to act on: `[close]` wins over `[>>]`, and within one
     * kind the smallest node wins (a nested label and its container usually
     * share the same text; clicking the leaf is what a finger would do).
     *
     * Full-screen nodes are rejected: the label may legitimately sit inside a
     * page-sized container, but that container must never be the thing clicked.
     */
    fun bestMatch(
        candidates: List<NodeSnapshot>,
        screenWidth: Int = 1080,
        screenHeight: Int = 2400
    ): AdActionMatch? {
        val screenArea = screenWidth.coerceAtLeast(1) * screenHeight.coerceAtLeast(1)
        val matches = candidates.mapNotNull { node ->
            if (!node.visible || node.width <= 0 || node.height <= 0) return@mapNotNull null
            if (node.area <= 0 || node.area > screenArea / 4) return@mapNotNull null
            val token = tokenOf(node) ?: return@mapNotNull null
            val kind = classify(token) ?: return@mapNotNull null
            AdActionMatch(kind, node, "TEXT_TOKEN_${kind.name}", token)
        }
        if (matches.isEmpty()) return null
        return matches.minWithOrNull(
            compareBy<AdActionMatch>({ if (it.kind == AdActionKind.CLOSE) 0 else 1 }, { it.node.area })
        )
    }

    /**
     * True when the control that would receive the tap is button-sized and sits
     * under the label.
     *
     * The click target is resolved at tap time and may be a clickable ancestor
     * of the label. An ancestor larger than 1/[MAX_TARGET_AREA_DIVISOR] of the
     * screen is the ad itself, and tapping it is an ad click that opens the
     * store (review 2026-11-02; the same rule as the close-button detector).
     */
    fun isSafeTapTarget(
        targetWidth: Int,
        targetHeight: Int,
        containsLabelCentre: Boolean,
        screenWidth: Int,
        screenHeight: Int
    ): Boolean {
        if (targetWidth <= 0 || targetHeight <= 0) return false
        if (!containsLabelCentre) return false
        val screenArea = screenWidth.coerceAtLeast(1).toLong() * screenHeight.coerceAtLeast(1)
        return targetWidth.toLong() * targetHeight <= screenArea / MAX_TARGET_AREA_DIVISOR
    }

    /** A tap target may cover at most 1/6 of the screen. */
    const val MAX_TARGET_AREA_DIVISOR = 6

    /** Trims, collapses inner whitespace and lower-cases a label. */
    internal fun normalize(label: String?): String? {
        val trimmed = label?.trim() ?: return null
        if (trimmed.isEmpty()) return null
        return trimmed.replace(Regex("\\s+"), " ").lowercase()
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.detector

/**
 * Classifies the activity a monitored reward app just brought to the front.
 *
 * This is the guard's ad-window signal (assessment item A4, option 1). The old
 * signal - "a close button was detected" - fired on ordinary app screens (a
 * news feed's dismiss icons kept ??撣?in AD_SESSION_ACTIVE for hours, so the
 * user's own switch to LINE was blocked and pulled back), and it never fired
 * for ads whose X is painted inside a WebView or a game engine canvas, so the
 * jumps those ads caused were never blocked.
 *
 * Rewarded and interstitial ads are shown by the ad SDK's own full-screen
 * activity, whose class name is public and stable. Measured on BitWalk (a
 * Flutter app whose only own activity is `jp.paddleinc.walk.MainActivity`):
 * every other declared activity belongs to an ad SDK.
 *
 * Pure Kotlin, no Android APIs, so it is unit tested directly.
 */
object AdActivityClassifier {

    enum class Kind {
        /** A full-screen ad is on screen. */
        AD,

        /**
         * An ad SDK's in-app browser / store page: the ad navigated away from
         * itself without leaving the reward app's task.
         */
        AD_LANDING,

        /** Anything else: the reward app's own UI, a login screen, a picker. */
        OTHER
    }

    fun classify(className: String?, sourcePackage: String?): Kind {
        val cls = className?.trim().orEmpty()
        if (cls.isEmpty() || '.' !in cls) return Kind.OTHER
        if (EXCLUDED_PREFIXES.any { cls.startsWith(it) }) return Kind.OTHER
        val simple = cls.substringAfterLast('.')
        if (DEBUG_TOKENS.any { simple.contains(it) }) return Kind.OTHER

        val knownSdk = AD_SDK_PREFIXES.any { cls.startsWith(it) }
        val ownClass = sourcePackage != null && isOwnClass(cls, sourcePackage)
        val tokens = camelTokens(simple)
        val adNamed = tokens.any { it in AD_TOKENS }

        // The reward app's own screens are never an ad on name alone: ??撣?has
        // `PersonalInfoCenterCustomAdActivity` (a settings page).
        if (!knownSdk && (ownClass || !adNamed)) return Kind.OTHER

        if (LANDING_TOKENS.any { simple.contains(it) } && !simple.contains("fullscreen", ignoreCase = true)) {
            return Kind.AD_LANDING
        }
        return Kind.AD
    }

    /**
     * True when [cls] lives in the reward app's own namespace, compared on the
     * first two package segments (`com.dongqiudi.news` owns `com.dongqiudi.*`).
     */
    private fun isOwnClass(cls: String, sourcePackage: String): Boolean {
        if (cls.startsWith("$sourcePackage.")) return true
        val root = sourcePackage.split('.').take(2).joinToString(".")
        return root.contains('.') && cls.startsWith("$root.")
    }

    /** `TTRewardVideoActivity` -> [TT, Reward, Video, Activity]. */
    internal fun camelTokens(simple: String): List<String> =
        Regex("[A-Z]+(?![a-z])|[A-Z][a-z0-9]*|[a-z0-9]+").findAll(simple).map { it.value }.toList()

    /** Words that only an ad activity carries as a whole CamelCase token. */
    private val AD_TOKENS = setOf("Ad", "Ads", "Rewarded", "Reward", "Interstitial", "Mraid", "Vast", "Playable")

    /** An ad SDK screen that is a web page or store page rather than the ad. */
    private val LANDING_TOKENS = listOf(
        "LandingPage", "Browser", "Website", "Webpage", "WebPage", "OpenUrl", "InlineStore", "StoreWebpage",
        "AppLovinWebView"
    )

    /** SDK test and debug screens are only ever opened on purpose. */
    private val DEBUG_TOKENS = listOf("Debugger", "TestSuite", "ReportAd", "AdReport", "Testing")

    /** Third-party screens that are not ads (login, payments, framework). */
    private val EXCLUDED_PREFIXES = listOf(
        "android.", "androidx.", "com.android.",
        "com.google.android.gms.auth.", "com.google.android.gms.common.",
        "com.google.android.play.core.", "com.google.firebase.",
        "com.facebook.FacebookActivity", "com.facebook.CustomTab",
        "io.flutter.", "com.pichillilorenzo.", "dev.fluttercommunity.",
        "com.braze.", "io.adjoe.", "com.alipay.", "com.tencent.connect.",
        "com.tencent.tauth.", "com.huawei.hms.", "com.sina.weibo."
    )

    /** Package prefixes of ad SDKs whose activities are always ad surfaces. */
    private val AD_SDK_PREFIXES = listOf(
        "com.google.android.gms.ads.",
        "com.applovin.adview.", "com.applovin.sdk.AppLovinWebViewActivity",
        "com.unity3d.ads.", "com.unity3d.services.ads.", "com.unity3d.ironsourceads.",
        "com.ironsource.sdk.controller.", "com.ironsource.mediationsdk.",
        "com.moloco.sdk.",
        "com.vungle.",
        "com.fyber.",
        "com.mbridge.msdk.", "com.mintegral.msdk.",
        "com.bytedance.sdk.openadsdk.", "com.pangle.",
        "com.inmobi.ads.",
        "com.facebook.ads.",
        "com.adcolony.sdk.",
        "com.chartboost.sdk.",
        "com.tapjoy.",
        "com.five_corp.ad.",
        "jp.maio.sdk.",
        "com.ogury.ad.",
        "com.my.target.",
        "com.yandex.mobile.ads.",
        "sg.bigo.ads.", "com.bigossp.",
        "com.smaato.", "net.pubnative.", "com.verve.",
        "com.amazon.device.ads.",
        "com.hyprmx.",
        "io.bidmachine.",
        "com.kwad.sdk.",
        "com.qq.e.ads.",
        "com.baidu.mobads.",
        "com.beizi.ad.",

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\detector\CloseButtonDetector.kt

package com.rewardadguard.app.detector

/**
 * Pure-Kotlin node snapshot so the close-button heuristics can be unit tested on
 * the JVM without an Android device.
 */
data class NodeSnapshot(
    val text: String?,
    val contentDescription: String?,
    val viewIdResourceName: String?,
    val className: String?,
    val clickable: Boolean,
    val left: Int,
    val top: Int,
    val right: Int,
    val bottom: Int,
    val visible: Boolean = true
) {
    val width: Int get() = (right - left).coerceAtLeast(0)
    val height: Int get() = (bottom - top).coerceAtLeast(0)
    val area: Int get() = width * height
}

/**
 * Result of matching a node against the close-button rules.
 */
data class CloseMatch(
    val matched: Boolean,
    val score: Int,
    val method: String,
    val node: NodeSnapshot?,
    val suggestedExpandedBounds: IntArray? = null
) {
    /** Human readable label such as "72x72", used by the log. */
    fun boundsLabel(): String {
        val b = suggestedExpandedBounds ?: return "-"
        return "${b[2] - b[0]}x${b[3] - b[1]}"
    }

    /**
     * Stable id that links the DETECTED -> DECIDED -> DISPATCHED -> VERIFIED rows
     * of one close-button event (P0#2), so a single X can be followed through the
     * whole pipeline instead of being four unrelated log lines.
     */
    fun correlationId(): String {
        val n = node ?: return "cid=none"
        return "cid=${n.left},${n.top},${n.right},${n.bottom}#$score"
    }

    /**
     * What the matched node is: view id, text, description and class. Score and
     * bounds alone could not tell a skip control from a store link afterwards
     * (InMobi tap followed by a store jump, 2026-11-04).
     */
    fun nodeLabel(): String {
        val n = node ?: return "node=none"
        fun clip(s: String?) = s?.replace('\n', ' ')?.take(NODE_LABEL_MAX) ?: "-"
        return "id=${clip(n.viewIdResourceName?.substringAfter(":id/"))} text=${clip(n.text)} " +
            "desc=${clip(n.contentDescription)} class=${clip(n.className?.substringAfterLast('.'))}"
    }

    private companion object {
        const val NODE_LABEL_MAX = 40
    }
}

/**
 * Detects an ad close ("X") control inside the current window tree
 * (spec sections 24-27).
 *
 * This object contains only the scoring / geometry logic; traversing the live
 * accessibility tree happens in the accessibility service. Keeping the decision
 * logic pure makes it unit-testable and reviewable.
 */
object CloseButtonDetector {

    /** Strong textual signals found in `text`, `contentDescription` or the view id. */
    private val STRONG_TEXT = setOf(
        "close", "close ad", "closead", "dismiss", "skip", "skip ad", "skipad",
        "??", "?喲", "頝喲?", "頝唾?", "??", "銝??渲閎"
    )

    /** Single glyphs that are almost always the ad X. */
    private val SYMBOL_TEXT = setOf(
        "x", "X", "?", "??, "??, "??, "漼?, "\u2715", "\u2716", "\u00D7"
    )

    private val WEAK_TEXT_TOKENS = listOf("close", "dismiss", "skip", "cancel", "exit")

    private val VIEW_ID_HINTS = listOf(
        "close", "dismiss", "skip", "ad_close", "adclose", "btn_close", "iv_close",
        "image_close", "close_btn", "closebutton", "ad_skip", "skip_view"
    )

    /**
     * Landing-page call-to-action phrases.
     *
     * These belong to the ad's *store* button, never to its X. Moloco ads draw a
     * "Google Play >>" CTA in the same top-right corner as the X, so without this
     * list the detector matches the CTA, the guard taps it, and the guard itself
     * produces the redirect it exists to prevent (field report 2026-10-16,
     * root cause 4.1). Matching is done on the normalised (lower-cased) text,
     * content description and view id, so it never fires on "Close"/"頝喲?".
     */
    private val STORE_CTA_TEXT = setOf(
        "install", "install now", "download", "download now", "get it on",
        "get it on google play", "google play", "play store", "learn more",
        "shop now", "buy now", "visit site", "visit website", "open in app",
        "銝?", "銝蝸", "蝡銝?", "蝡銝蝸", "摰?", "摰?", "蝡摰?", "蝡摰?",
        "??", "蝡??", "????", "鞈潸眺", "韐凋僭", "鈭圾?游?", "??", "??",
        "?脣?", "?瑕?", "?祥??"
    )

    /** View-id fragments that mark a store CTA rather than an X. */
    private val STORE_CTA_ID_HINTS = listOf(
        "cta", "install", "download", "google_play", "playstore", "play_store",
        "get_it_on", "learn_more", "shop_now", "buy_now", "visit_site"
    )

    private val CLOSE_CLASSES = setOf(
        "android.widget.ImageButton",
        "android.widget.ImageView",
        "android.widget.Button",
        "android.widget.TextView",
        "androidx.appcompat.widget.AppCompatImageButton",
        "androidx.appcompat.widget.AppCompatImageView"
    )

    /**
     * Scores a single node snapshot.
     *
     * @param screenWidth / [screenHeight] are used to reject nodes that cannot be
     *        the small corner X of an ad (a full-screen "close" CTA is not it).
     */
    fun score(
        node: NodeSnapshot,
        screenWidth: Int = 1080,
        screenHeight: Int = 2400
    ): CloseMatch {
        if (!node.visible) return CloseMatch(false, 0, "INVISIBLE", node)
        if (node.width <= 0 || node.height <= 0) return CloseMatch(false, 0, "ZERO_BOUNDS", node)

        val text = node.text?.trim()
        val desc = node.contentDescription?.trim()
        val normalizedText = text?.lowercase()
        val normalizedDesc = desc?.lowercase()
        val normalizedId = node.viewIdResourceName?.lowercase().orEmpty()

        // 0. A store / install call to action is never the ad's X, whatever its
        //    geometry or view id says. Rejected before scoring so it can never
        //    accumulate the corner + class + id points that used to make a
        //    "Google Play >>" button look like a close control.
        if (isStoreCta(normalizedText, normalizedDesc, normalizedId)) {
            return CloseMatch(false, 0, "REJECTED_CTA", node)
        }

        var score = 0
        var method = "NONE"

        // 1. Exact glyph ("x", "?", "??) -> strongest signal.
        if (text in SYMBOL_TEXT || desc in SYMBOL_TEXT) {
            score += 60
            method = "SYMBOL_TEXT"
        }

        // 2. Exact strong keyword.
        if (normalizedText != null && STRONG_TEXT.contains(normalizedText)) {
            score += 55
            if (method == "NONE") method = "TEXT_KEYWORD"
        }
        if (normalizedDesc != null && STRONG_TEXT.contains(normalizedDesc)) {
            score += 55
            if (method == "NONE") method = "DESCRIPTION_KEYWORD"
        }

        // 3. Weak tokens inside longer strings ("Tap to close the ad").
        val weakHit = WEAK_TEXT_TOKENS.any { token ->
            normalizedText?.contains(token) == true || normalizedDesc?.contains(token) == true
        }
        if (weakHit && method == "NONE") {
            score += 25
            method = "TEXT_HINT"
        }

        // 4. View id hints.
        if (VIEW_ID_HINTS.any { normalizedId.contains(it) }) {
            score += 40
            if (method == "NONE") method = "VIEW_ID"
        }

        // 5. Geometry: ad close controls live in a corner and are small.
        val cornerBonus = cornerScore(node, screenWidth, screenHeight)
        if (cornerBonus > 0) {
            score += cornerBonus
            if (method == "NONE") method = "CORNER_GEOMETRY"
        }

        // 6. Class sanity.
        if (node.className in CLOSE_CLASSES) score += 5

        // 7. Penalty: a huge clickable area is normally a CTA, not the X.
        if (node.area > (screenWidth * screenHeight) / 6) score -= 25

        val matched = score >= MATCH_THRESHOLD
        return CloseMatch(
            matched = matched,
            score = score,
            method = if (matched) method else "REJECTED_SCORE_$score",
            node = node,
            suggestedExpandedBounds = if (matched) expandedBounds(node, DEFAULT_SCALE) else null
        )
    }

    /** Picks the best match out of a candidate list, or null when none matched. */
    fun bestMatch(
        candidates: List<NodeSnapshot>,
        screenWidth: Int = 1080,
        screenHeight: Int = 2400
    ): CloseMatch? = candidates
        .map { score(it, screenWidth, screenHeight) }
        .filter { it.matched }
        .maxByOrNull { it.score }

    /**
     * Computes the click target the guard *suggests* for a matched node.
     *
     * IMPORTANT (spec section 26): a non-root app cannot resize a third-party
     * view. This method therefore only computes geometry that the service may
     * use for an assisted/expanded accessibility action. It never modifies the
     * other app's layout.
     */
    fun expandedBounds(node: NodeSnapshot, scale: Float): IntArray {
        val safeScale = scale.coerceIn(1f, 5f)
        if (safeScale == 1f) return intArrayOf(node.left, node.top, node.right, node.bottom)

        val cx = (node.left + node.right) / 2
        val cy = (node.top + node.bottom) / 2
        val halfWidth = (node.width * safeScale / 2f).toInt().coerceAtLeast(node.width / 2)
        val halfHeight = (node.height * safeScale / 2f).toInt().coerceAtLeast(node.height / 2)
        return intArrayOf(
            (cx - halfWidth).coerceAtLeast(0),
            (cy - halfHeight).coerceAtLeast(0),
            cx + halfWidth,
            cy + halfHeight
        )
    }

    /** Corner proximity + smallness bonus. */
    private fun cornerScore(node: NodeSnapshot, screenWidth: Int, screenHeight: Int): Int {
        val cx = (node.left + node.right) / 2
        val cy = (node.top + node.bottom) / 2
        val horizontalEdge = cx < screenWidth / 4 || cx > screenWidth * 3 / 4
        val verticalEdge = cy < screenHeight / 3 || cy > screenHeight * 2 / 3
        val small = node.width <= screenWidth / 6 && node.height <= screenHeight / 12
        var score = 0
        if (horizontalEdge) score += 12
        if (verticalEdge) score += 8
        if (small) score += 10
        return score
    }

    /**
     * True when any of the node's own labels describe a store / install CTA.
     *
     * Text and description are substring-matched (an ad renders "Google Play >>",
     * which no exact-match list would ever contain); the view id is
     * substring-matched too. The phrases are CTA-specific, so a genuine
     * Close/Skip control never trips this.
     */
    private fun isStoreCta(
        normalizedText: String?,
        normalizedDesc: String?,
        normalizedId: String
    ): Boolean {
        if (normalizedText != null && STORE_CTA_TEXT.any { normalizedText.contains(it) }) return true
        if (normalizedDesc != null && STORE_CTA_TEXT.any { normalizedDesc.contains(it) }) return true
        return STORE_CTA_ID_HINTS.any { normalizedId.contains(it) }
    }

    /** Scores at or above this value are treated as an ad close control. */
    const val MATCH_THRESHOLD = 45

    /**
     * True when a matched node looks like a close control that is safe to *tap*.
     *
     * Detection stays generous; clicking does not. BitWalk test 2026-11-02: all
     * six store jumps in 33 minutes came 0.5-1.6 s after the guard's own
     * assisted tap, on matches scoring 50-80:
     *  - Moloco "Google Play >>" 381x99 and a Unity text block 300x84 (wide),
     *  - a Fyber call-to-action 123x72 (aspect 1.7),
     *  - an InMobi control 72x75 centred at y=1267, mid-screen.
     * Every real X that closed an ad that day was roughly square (aspect
     * 0.98-1.3) and centred in the top 300 px. So a tap needs a near-square node
     * fully on screen in the top [ASSIST_TOP_BAND] of the screen.
     */
    fun isPlausibleAssistTarget(node: NodeSnapshot, screenWidth: Int, screenHeight: Int): Boolean {
        if (node.width <= 0 || node.height <= 0) return false
        if (node.left < 0 || node.top < 0 || node.right > screenWidth || node.bottom > screenHeight) return false
        val aspect = node.width.toFloat() / node.height
        if (aspect > MAX_ASSIST_ASPECT || aspect < 1f / MAX_ASSIST_ASPECT) return false
        val centreY = (node.top + node.bottom) / 2
        return centreY <= screenHeight * ASSIST_TOP_BAND
    }

    /** Width/height (or height/width) above this is a text button, not an X. */
    const val MAX_ASSIST_ASPECT = 1.5f

    /** Fraction of the screen height, from the top, where a tappable X may sit. */
    const val ASSIST_TOP_BAND = 0.2f

    /** Default expansion used when no user preference is available. */
    const val DEFAULT_SCALE = 3f
}

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\detector\ForegroundAppDetector.kt
==============================================================================
package com.rewardadguard.app.detector

import android.content.Context
import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityEvent
import android.view.accessibility.AccessibilityWindowInfo

/**
 * Answers one question: which package is in the foreground right now?
 *
 * Strategy (no polling):
 *  1. `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` carries the package name for the window that
 *     just became active, which is the cheapest and most reliable signal.
 *  2. If that is missing or is our own app / the system UI, the active window is
 *     taken from [AccessibilityService.windows] (our own IME and system overlays
 *     are filtered out).
 *
 * The detector keeps the previous package so that transitions can be logged as
 * `SOURCE -> DESTINATION` (spec section 12).
 */
class ForegroundAppDetector(private val context: Context) {

    data class ForegroundChange(
        val previousPackage: String?,
        val currentPackage: String?,
        /** Where the package name came from, for the log. */
        val detectionMethod: String
    ) {
        val changed: Boolean
            get() = currentPackage != null && currentPackage != previousPackage
    }

    @Volatile
    var currentPackage: String? = null
        private set

    @Volatile
    var previousPackage: String? = null
        private set

    /** Resolves the package for [event] with a fallback to the active window. */
    fun resolve(
        eventPackage: String?,
        activeWindowPackage: String?
    ): ForegroundChange {
        val fromEvent = eventPackage?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() && it != SYSTEM_UI }
        val resolved = fromEvent
            ?: activeWindowPackage?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() && it != SYSTEM_UI }
            ?: currentPackage

        val method = when {
            fromEvent != null -> "EVENT_PACKAGE"
            activeWindowPackage != null -> "ACTIVE_WINDOW"
            else -> "CACHED_PACKAGE"
        }

        val previous = currentPackage
        return ForegroundChange(
            previousPackage = previous,
            currentPackage = resolved,
            detectionMethod = method
        ).also {
            if (it.changed) {
                previousPackage = previous
                currentPackage = resolved
            }
        }
    }

    /** Extracts the package of the currently focused window, if any. */
    fun activeWindowPackage(windows: List<AccessibilityWindowInfo>?): String? {
        if (windows.isNullOrEmpty()) return null
        val candidates = windows.asSequence()
            .filter { it.type == AccessibilityWindowInfo.TYPE_APPLICATION }
            .filter { it.isActive || it.isFocused }
        val fallback = windows.asSequence().filter { it.type == AccessibilityWindowInfo.TYPE_APPLICATION }
        val window = (candidates.firstOrNull() ?: fallback.firstOrNull()) ?: return null
        return try {
            window.root?.packageName?.toString()
        } catch (t: Throwable) {
            null
        } finally {
            @Suppress("DEPRECATION")
            runCatching { window.recycle() }
        }
    }

    fun isFrom(event: AccessibilityEvent): Boolean =
        event.packageName?.toString() == context.packageName

    companion object {
        private const val SYSTEM_UI = "com.android.systemui"
    }
}

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\detector\PackageClassifier.kt
==============================================================================
package com.rewardadguard.app.detector

import android.content.Context
import android.content.Intent
import android.content.pm.PackageManager
import android.util.Log
import com.rewardadguard.app.data.EventType

/**
 * Classifies an external destination package or URI.
 *
 * Deliberately NOT a blacklist: nothing here names "Shopee" or "Google Play" as
 * a forbidden target. Classification only describes *what kind of* destination
 * was reached, and the decision to block is made by
 * [com.rewardadguard.app.guard.RedirectGuard] from the source/session context.
 */
class PackageClassifier(private val context: Context) {

    private val packageManager: PackageManager = context.packageManager

    /**
     * The current launcher, resolved once. The hot foreground path asks this on
     * every transition, so the PackageManager binder call must not repeat.
     */
    private val homePackage: String? by lazy {
        try {
            val home = Intent(Intent.ACTION_MAIN).addCategory(Intent.CATEGORY_HOME)
            packageManager.resolveActivity(home, PackageManager.MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY)
                ?.activityInfo?.packageName
        } catch (t: Throwable) {
            null
        }
    }

    /**
     * @param destinationPackage the package that took the foreground, if known
     * @param referrerUriScheme scheme of the URI that was being handled, if known
     */
    fun classify(destinationPackage: String?, referrerUriScheme: String? = null): DestinationKind {
        val pkg = destinationPackage?.trim().orEmpty()

        if (pkg.isEmpty()) {
            return DestinationKind.UNKNOWN
        }

        if (pkg == context.packageName) return DestinationKind.SELF

        // The home screen, system UI or an IME in the foreground is the user
        // leaving on purpose, never an ad redirect. Treating a Home press as a
        // redirect made the guard block it and then relaunch the reward app, so
        // the reward app appeared to "keep popping up" every couple of seconds.
        if (isSystemSurface(pkg)) return DestinationKind.UNKNOWN

        val launcherIntent = packageManager.getLaunchIntentForPackage(pkg)

        // Browsers: a VIEW/https handler that is also a launcher app.
        val browser = launcherIntent != null && isBrowser(pkg)
        if (browser) return DestinationKind.BROWSER

        if (isStore(pkg, referrerUriScheme)) return DestinationKind.STORE

        if (isGame(pkg)) return DestinationKind.GAME

        if (DEEP_LINK_HINTS.any { pkg.contains(it, ignoreCase = true) }) {
            return DestinationKind.DEEP_LINK
        }

        return DestinationKind.EXTERNAL_APP
    }

    /** True when the app resolves an https VIEW intent (i.e. it is a browser). */
    private fun isBrowser(packageName: String): Boolean = try {
        val intent = Intent(Intent.ACTION_VIEW, android.net.Uri.parse("https://example.com"))
        val handlers = packageManager.queryIntentActivities(intent, PackageManager.MATCH_DEFAULT_ONLY)
        handlers.any { it.activityInfo?.packageName == packageName } || packageName in KNOWN_BROWSERS
    } catch (t: Throwable) {
        Log.w(TAG, "isBrowser failed for $packageName", t)
        packageName in KNOWN_BROWSERS
    }

    private fun isStore(packageName: String, scheme: String?): Boolean =
        scheme == "market" || packageName in KNOWN_STORES

    private fun isGame(packageName: String): Boolean = try {
        val info = packageManager.getApplicationInfo(packageName, 0)
        (info.category == android.content.pm.ApplicationInfo.CATEGORY_GAME) ||
            GAME_HINTS.any { packageName.contains(it, ignoreCase = true) }
    } catch (t: Throwable) {
        Log.w(TAG, "isGame failed for $packageName", t)
        false
    }

    /**
     * True for the current home app, the system UI and IMEs.
     *
     * The home app is resolved from the HOME intent, so a third-party launcher is
     * recognised even without a telltale package name (mirrors AllowlistGuard).
     */
    private fun isSystemSurface(packageName: String): Boolean {
        if (SystemOverlayPackages.isSystemSurface(packageName)) return true
        val lower = packageName.lowercase()
        if (LAUNCHER_HINTS.any { lower.contains(it) }) return true
        if (IME_HINTS.any { lower.contains(it) }) return true
        return homePackage == packageName
    }

    /**
     * True when [packageName] is the user's current home/launcher surface.
     *
     * Resolved through the HOME intent rather than a name list so a third-party
     * launcher is recognised too. Used to tell "the user went Home on purpose"
     * (end the session) from "the ad opened another app" (chase it).
     */
    fun isHomePackage(packageName: String): Boolean = homePackage == packageName

    /** Maps a classification to the loggable event type. */
    fun eventTypeFor(kind: DestinationKind): EventType = when (kind) {
        DestinationKind.BROWSER -> EventType.BROWSER
        DestinationKind.STORE -> EventType.STORE
        DestinationKind.GAME -> EventType.GAME
        DestinationKind.DEEP_LINK -> EventType.DEEP_LINK
        else -> EventType.EXTERNAL_APP
    }

    companion object {
        private const val TAG = "PackageClassifier"

        private val KNOWN_BROWSERS = setOf(
            "com.android.chrome",
            "com.chrome.beta",
            "com.chrome.dev",
            "com.chrome.canary",
            "org.mozilla.firefox",
            "org.mozilla.firefox_beta",
            "com.brave.browser",
            "com.microsoft.emmx",
            "com.opera.browser",
            "com.opera.mini.native",
            "com.sec.android.app.sbrowser",
            "com.miui.browser",
            "com.android.browser",
            "com.quark.browser",
            "com.UCMobile.intl",
            "com.heytap.browser",
            "com.vivo.browser"
        )

        private val KNOWN_STORES = setOf(
            "com.android.vending",
            "com.google.android.finsky",
            "com.huawei.appmarket",
            "com.xiaomi.market",
            "com.sec.android.app.samsungapps",
            "com.oppo.market",
            "com.heytap.market",
            "com.bbk.appstore",
            "com.amazon.venezia",
            "com.aptoide.partners"
        )

        private val LAUNCHER_HINTS = listOf("launcher", "home", "oneplus.launcher")
        private val IME_HINTS = listOf("inputmethod", "keyboard", "gboard", "swiftkey", "sogou", "ime")

        private val GAME_HINTS = listOf("game", "play.games", "minigame")
        private val DEEP_LINK_HINTS = listOf("deeplink", "shortlink", "redirect")
    }
}

/** Destination classes reported to the log and the UI. */
enum class DestinationKind {
    SELF,
    BROWSER,
    STORE,
    GAME,
    DEEP_LINK,
    EXTERNAL_APP,
    UNKNOWN;

    val isExternal: Boolean
        get() = this != SELF && this != UNKNOWN
}

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\detector\RedirectDetector.kt
==============================================================================
package com.rewardadguard.app.detector

import android.content.Context
import com.rewardadguard.app.manager.RewardAppStore

/**
 * Core source-based rule (spec sections 16-17).
 *
 * A redirect is only ever considered when ALL of the following hold:
 *  1. the *previous* foreground package is one of the user's selected reward apps,
 *  2. a reward session is active for that package,
 *  3. the foreground package changed,
 *  4. the new package is not the source package itself.
 *
 * Consequence: `Chrome -> Play Store`, `LINE -> Chrome` and `Chrome -> Game` are
 * never classified as redirects, because Chrome/LINE are not monitored sources.
 */
class RedirectDetector(
    private val context: Context,
    private val rewardAppStore: RewardAppStore,
    private val classifier: PackageClassifier
) {

    data class Detection(
        val sourcePackage: String,
        val destinationPackage: String,
        val kind: DestinationKind,
        val detectionMethod: String
    ) {
        val isExternal: Boolean get() = kind.isExternal
    }

    /**
     * @param previousPackage foreground package before the change
     * @param currentPackage  foreground package after the change
     * @param sessionSourcePackage the package the running session belongs to
     * @param sessionActive whether a reward session is currently running
     * @param uriScheme optional scheme of the URI that triggered the transition
     * @param chainedRedirect true when the service already established that this
     *        is a later hop of the ad's chain (the immediately previous package
     *        is then another external app, not the reward app)
     */
    fun detect(
        previousPackage: String?,
        currentPackage: String?,
        sessionSourcePackage: String?,
        sessionActive: Boolean,
        uriScheme: String? = null,
        chainedRedirect: Boolean = false
    ): Detection? {
        if (!sessionActive || sessionSourcePackage == null) return null
        if (currentPackage == null || previousPackage == null) return null
        if (currentPackage == previousPackage) return null

        // (1) the session source must be the app we are leaving; a later hop of
        // the same chain is allowed when the caller has already tracked the
        // departure (field report 2026-10-30: resolver/island between the ad and
        // Shopee used to hide the transition entirely).
        if (previousPackage != sessionSourcePackage && !chainedRedirect) return null

        // (2) the session source must still be a monitored reward app
        if (!rewardAppStore.isMonitored(sessionSourcePackage)) return null

        // (3) our own UI taking the foreground is not an external redirect
        if (currentPackage == context.packageName) return null

        // (4) the destination must actually differ from the source
        if (currentPackage == sessionSourcePackage) return null

        val kind = classifier.classify(currentPackage, uriScheme)
        if (kind == DestinationKind.SELF || kind == DestinationKind.UNKNOWN) return null

        return Detection(
            sourcePackage = sessionSourcePackage,
            destinationPackage = currentPackage,
            kind = kind,
            detectionMethod = if (chainedRedirect) "REDIRECT_CHAIN" else "SOURCE_BASED_FOREGROUND_TRANSITION"
        )
    }
}

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\detector\SystemOverlayPackages.kt
==============================================================================
package com.rewardadguard.app.detector

/**
 * Packages that draw system surfaces but are never "the app the user is in".
 *
 * Field report 2026-10-30: on HyperOS the dynamic island
 * (`miui.systemui.plugin`) raises `TYPE_WINDOW_STATE_CHANGED` like a normal app.
 * Treating it as the foreground app made the guard (a) schedule a Back press
 * while the reward app never left, closing it, and (b) overwrite the "previous"
 * package, so the Shopee app opened afterwards was no longer recognised as an
 * ad redirect. The intent resolver is the same class of surface: it only hands
 * the URI over to the real destination.
 *
 * The list is explicit on purpose. Substring matching on "plugin" or "resolver"
 * would misclassify ordinary apps, and every consumer must agree on exactly the
 * same set.
 */
object SystemOverlayPackages {

    /** Surfaces that must never become the foreground package. */
    private val OVERLAYS = setOf(
        "com.android.systemui",
        "miui.systemui.plugin",
        "com.android.intentresolver"
    )

    /**
     * Everything that is a system surface for policy purposes: the overlays
     * above plus settings, permission dialogs and package installers. The guard
     * must neither start a session for them nor treat them as a destination.
     */
    private val SYSTEM_SURFACES = OVERLAYS + setOf(
        "com.android.settings",
        "android",
        "com.google.android.permissioncontroller",
        "com.android.permissioncontroller",
        "com.google.android.packageinstaller",
        "com.android.packageinstaller"
    )

    /**
     * Tools the user summons on top of whatever is on screen: Google search /
     * Circle to Search / Assistant, Gemini and Lens.
     *
     * 2026-11-04: during AHEALTH ads the Google app came to the front straight
     * from the reward app five times without any tap by the guard - the user
     * calling up search or Assistant while waiting - and the guard took it for
     * an ad redirect and pressed Back, closing it. Ads open Chrome or the Play
     * Store, not these; they are treated like the launcher: the user leaving on
     * purpose.
     */
    private val USER_SUMMONED = setOf(
        "com.google.android.googlequicksearchbox",
        "com.google.android.apps.googleassistant",
        "com.google.android.apps.bard",
        "com.google.ar.lens"
    )

    /** True for [USER_SUMMONED] tools, which must never be blocked. */
    fun isUserSummoned(packageName: String): Boolean = packageName in USER_SUMMONED

    /** True for floating system windows that sit above the real foreground app. */
    fun isOverlay(packageName: String): Boolean = packageName in OVERLAYS

    /** True for overlays and the other system surfaces listed above. */
    fun isSystemSurface(packageName: String): Boolean = packageName in SYSTEM_SURFACES
}

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\guard\AdActionGuard.kt
==============================================================================
package com.rewardadguard.app.guard

import com.rewardadguard.app.data.AppSettings
import com.rewardadguard.app.data.AssistAction
import com.rewardadguard.app.data.EventType
import com.rewardadguard.app.detector.AdActionKind
import com.rewardadguard.app.detector.AdActionMatch
import com.rewardadguard.app.manager.EventLogger
import com.rewardadguard.app.session.SessionManager

/**
 * Why an ad-page action (`[close]` / `[>>]` / `[->]`) was not dispatched.
 *
 * Named reasons instead of a bare `Boolean` so the log can tell a deliberate
 * setting (`AssistAction.NONE`) from a safety rejection (the reward app is not
 * the verified foreground app) and from a temporary throttle.
 */
enum class AdActionDecision {
    /** The action may be dispatched. */
    ALLOW,

    /** Close-button assistance is switched off in settings. */
    DISABLED,

    /** Detect-only mode: log, never click. */
    ACTION_NONE,

    /** Not inside a verified ad window of a monitored reward app. */
    NOT_AD_WINDOW,

    /** The foreground package could not be resolved, so nothing may be clicked. */
    FOREGROUND_UNKNOWN,

    /** The foreground app is not the reward app that owns this ad. */
    FOREGROUND_MISMATCH,

    /** A real finger is on the screen. */
    USER_INTERACTING,

    /** Another ad action was dispatched too recently. */
    THROTTLED,

    /** The same control on the same screen was already clicked. */
    REPEATED,

    /** The per-ad cap of next-step clicks was reached. */
    NEXT_CAP,

    /** No clickable target could be resolved on top of the labelled node. */
    NOT_OPERABLE;

    /** True when the guard actively chose not to click (not a failure). */
    val isDeliberate: Boolean
        get() = this == DISABLED || this == ACTION_NONE

    fun describe(): String = when (this) {
        ALLOW -> "allowed"
        DISABLED -> "close button assistance disabled in settings"
        ACTION_NONE -> "assist action is NONE (detect only, never click)"
        NOT_AD_WINDOW -> "no verified ad window of a monitored reward app"
        FOREGROUND_UNKNOWN -> "foreground package could not be verified"
        FOREGROUND_MISMATCH -> "foreground app is not the reward app that owns the ad"
        USER_INTERACTING -> "user is touching the screen"
        THROTTLED -> "throttled: another ad action is within ${AdActionGuard.THROTTLE_MILLIS}ms"
        REPEATED -> "the same control was already clicked on this screen"
        NEXT_CAP -> "per-ad next-step cap reached (${AdActionGuard.MAX_NEXT_STEPS_PER_AD})"
        NOT_OPERABLE -> "no clickable target on top of the label"
    }
}

/**
 * Safety policy for the literal `[close]` and `[>>]` / `[->]` ad controls.
 *
 * Two invariants are enforced before any click:
 *  1. the ad window belongs to a monitored reward app **and** the foreground
 *     package is exactly that app - a normal app can never be clicked, even if
 *     its screen contains the same labels;
 *  2. one click per [THROTTLE_MILLIS], the same labelled control is not clicked
 *     twice while it stays on screen, and at most [MAX_NEXT_STEPS_PER_AD] step
 *     clicks per ad so a looping ad cannot be chased forever.
 *
 * The collaborator references are nullable for the same reason as
 * [CloseButtonGuard]: [decide] must be testable on the JVM without Room.
 */
class AdActionGuard(
    private val logger: EventLogger?,
    private val sessionManager: SessionManager?
) {

    private var lastDispatchAt: Long = 0L
    private var lastKey: String? = null
    private var nextStepsThisAd: Int = 0

    /** Last deliberate (settings) skip that was written, for de-duplication. */
    private var lastDeliberateKey: String? = null
    private var lastDeliberateAt: Long = 0L

    /**
     * @param adWindowMonitored the ad window belongs to a monitored reward app
     * @param rootPackageMatches the live window's root really is [expectedPackage]
     * @param foregroundPackage the package actually in the foreground right now
     * @param expectedPackage the monitored reward app that owns the ad
     */
    fun decide(
        match: AdActionMatch,
        settings: AppSettings,
        adWindowMonitored: Boolean,
        rootPackageMatches: Boolean,
        foregroundPackage: String?,
        expectedPackage: String?,
        userInteracting: Boolean,
        now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
    ): AdActionDecision {
        if (!settings.closeButtonAssistance) return AdActionDecision.DISABLED
        if (settings.assistAction == AssistAction.NONE) return AdActionDecision.ACTION_NONE
        if (!adWindowMonitored) return AdActionDecision.NOT_AD_WINDOW
        if (foregroundPackage.isNullOrBlank()) return AdActionDecision.FOREGROUND_UNKNOWN
        if (expectedPackage.isNullOrBlank() || !rootPackageMatches ||
            foregroundPackage != expectedPackage
        ) {
            return AdActionDecision.FOREGROUND_MISMATCH
        }
        if (userInteracting) return AdActionDecision.USER_INTERACTING
        if (now - lastDispatchAt < THROTTLE_MILLIS) return AdActionDecision.THROTTLED
        // The same control (same token on the same rectangle) is never clicked
        // twice until the screen actually changed: a new control, no control at
        // all, or a verified successful click clears the key.
        if (keyOf(match) == lastKey) return AdActionDecision.REPEATED
        if (match.kind == AdActionKind.NEXT && nextStepsThisAd >= MAX_NEXT_STEPS_PER_AD) {
            return AdActionDecision.NEXT_CAP
        }
        return AdActionDecision.ALLOW
    }

    /** Records a dispatched action and its (unverified) outcome. */
    fun onDispatched(
        match: AdActionMatch,
        ownerPackage: String?,
        now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
    ) {
        lastDispatchAt = now
        lastKey = keyOf(match)
        if (match.kind == AdActionKind.NEXT) nextStepsThisAd++
        logger?.log(
            eventType = EventType.AD_ACTION,
            sessionId = sessionId(),
            sourcePackage = ownerPackage,
            detectionMethod = match.method,
            action = if (match.kind == AdActionKind.CLOSE) "AD_CLOSE_CLICK" else "AD_NEXT_CLICK",
            // DISPATCHED, not SUCCESS: the click was sent; [onVerified] decides
            // whether the control actually went away.
            result = "DISPATCHED",
            message = "token=${match.token} bounds=${match.boundsLabel()} ${match.correlationId()}",
            timestamp = now
        )
    }

    /**
     * Records that an action was refused, naming the reason.
     *
     * Throttle and repeat rejections are not logged: they fire on every content
     * change while the same control stays on screen and would flood the log.
     * A deliberate setting (detect-only) fires just as often, so it is written
     * once per control and then at most every [DELIBERATE_LOG_INTERVAL_MILLIS]
     * (review 2026-11-02: one row per scan, about two rows a second).
     */
    fun onSkipped(
        decision: AdActionDecision,
        match: AdActionMatch,
        ownerPackage: String?,
        now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
    ) {
        if (!shouldLogSkip(decision, match, now)) return
        logger?.log(
            eventType = EventType.AD_ACTION,
            sessionId = sessionId(),
            sourcePackage = ownerPackage,
            detectionMethod = match.method,
            action = "AD_ACTION_SKIPPED_${decision.name}",
            result = "SKIPPED",
            message = decision.describe(),
            timestamp = now
        )
    }

    /**
     * True when a skipped [decision] deserves a log row; records it when so.
     *
     * Separate from [onSkipped] so the de-duplication is testable without a
     * database-backed [EventLogger].
     */
    internal fun shouldLogSkip(decision: AdActionDecision, match: AdActionMatch, now: Long): Boolean {
        if (decision == AdActionDecision.ALLOW) return false
        if (decision == AdActionDecision.THROTTLED || decision == AdActionDecision.REPEATED) return false
        if (decision.isDeliberate) {
            val key = "${decision.name}|${keyOf(match)}"
            if (key == lastDeliberateKey && now - lastDeliberateAt < DELIBERATE_LOG_INTERVAL_MILLIS) return false
            lastDeliberateKey = key
            lastDeliberateAt = now
        }
        return true
    }

    /** Records whether the clicked control actually disappeared. */
    fun onVerified(
        match: AdActionMatch,
        verified: Boolean,
        ownerPackage: String?,
        now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
    ) {
        // A verified click means the screen moved on, so the same coordinates may
        // legitimately carry the next step's control again.
        if (verified) lastKey = null
        logger?.log(
            eventType = EventType.AD_ACTION,
            sessionId = sessionId(),
            sourcePackage = ownerPackage,
            detectionMethod = match.method,
            action = if (match.kind == AdActionKind.CLOSE) "AD_CLOSE_RESULT" else "AD_NEXT_RESULT",
            result = if (verified) "VERIFIED" else "UNKNOWN",
            message = "token=${match.token} bounds=${match.boundsLabel()} ${match.correlationId()}",
            timestamp = now
        )
    }

    /**
     * Called when a scan sees no `[close]` / `[>>]` / `[->]` control at all.
     *
     * The screen no longer shows the control that was last clicked, so the same
     * rectangle may be used again by the next ad page.
     */
    fun onScreenCleared() {
        lastKey = null
    }

    /** Clears throttle/cap state; called when an ad session starts or ends. */
    fun reset() {
        lastDispatchAt = 0L
        lastKey = null
        nextStepsThisAd = 0
        lastDeliberateKey = null
        lastDeliberateAt = 0L
    }

    /** How many next-step clicks this ad has used, for the debug dump. */
    val nextSteps: Int get() = nextStepsThisAd

    /** Milliseconds left before another action may be dispatched. */
    fun millisUntilThrottleClears(now: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()): Long =
        (lastDispatchAt + THROTTLE_MILLIS - now).coerceAtLeast(0L)

    private fun keyOf(match: AdActionMatch): String =
        "${match.token}@${match.node.left},${match.node.top},${match.node.right},${match.node.bottom}"

    private fun sessionId(): String =
        sessionManager?.currentSessionId ?: EventLogger.NO_SESSION

    companion object {
        /** Minimum gap between two ad-page actions. */
        const val THROTTLE_MILLIS = 800L

        /** Hard cap on `[>>]` / `[->]` clicks inside one ad. */
        const val MAX_NEXT_STEPS_PER_AD = 8

        /** One detect-only row per control per this interval, like CLOSE_DETECT. */
        const val DELIBERATE_LOG_INTERVAL_MILLIS = 10_000L
    }
}

package com.rewardadguard.app.guard

import com.rewardadguard.app.data.EventType
import com.rewardadguard.app.detector.SystemOverlayPackages
import com.rewardadguard.app.manager.EventLogger
import com.rewardadguard.app.manager.RewardAppStore
import com.rewardadguard.app.session.SessionManager

/**
 * Final safety net in front of every guard action (spec section 31).
 *
 * It answers one question: "is the guard allowed to act at all right now?"
 *
 * Reasons the guard must stay passive:
 *  - the app was disabled by the user,
 *  - the foreground app is not a monitored reward app,
 *  - the system UI / launcher / an IME owns the screen,
 *  - the user explicitly told us to ignore this package.
 */
class AllowlistGuard(
    private val rewardAppStore: RewardAppStore,
    private val logger: EventLogger,
    private val sessionManager: SessionManager
) {

    /** Protection scopes, in the order they are consulted. */
    enum class Scope {
        /** The source app is monitored and the session belongs to it. */
        MONITORED_SOURCE,

        /** Foreground app is not monitored -> passive. */
        NOT_MONITORED,

        /** The system UI, launcher or an input method -> passive. */
        SYSTEM_SURFACE,

        /** The user's own package ignore list -> passive. */
        IGNORED_PACKAGE,

        /** Protection disabled in settings -> passive. */
        DISABLED
    }

    fun evaluate(
        foregroundPackage: String?,
        protectionEnabled: Boolean,
        sourcePackage: String? = null
    ): Scope {
        if (!protectionEnabled) return Scope.DISABLED
        val pkg = foregroundPackage ?: return Scope.NOT_MONITORED
        if (isSystemSurface(pkg)) return Scope.SYSTEM_SURFACE
        if (rewardAppStore.isIgnored(pkg)) return Scope.IGNORED_PACKAGE
        if (sourcePackage != null && pkg == sourcePackage) return Scope.MONITORED_SOURCE
        return if (rewardAppStore.isMonitored(pkg)) Scope.MONITORED_SOURCE else Scope.NOT_MONITORED
    }

    fun canAct(scope: Scope): Boolean = scope == Scope.MONITORED_SOURCE

    /**
     * Logs a blocked-by-policy decision once, so the log explains *why* nothing
     * happened even though an ad was on screen.
     */
    /** Logs a blocked-by-policy decision once, so the log explains *why* nothing
     * happened even though an ad was on screen.
     */
    fun logPassive(scope: Scope, foregroundPackage: String?, reason: String) {
        logger.log(
            eventType = EventType.EXTRA_INFO,
            sessionId = sessionManager.currentSessionId ?: EventLogger.NO_SESSION,
            sourcePackage = foregroundPackage,
            detectionMethod = scope.name,
            action = "PASSIVE",
            result = "SKIPPED",
            message = reason
        )
    }

    companion object {
        private val LAUNCHER_HINTS = listOf(
            "launcher", "home", "oneplus.launcher"
        )

        private val IME_HINTS = listOf(
            "inputmethod", "keyboard", "gboard", "swiftkey", "sogou", "ime"
        )

        /**
         * True for the status bar, launchers, IMEs and system dialogs.
         *
         * A launcher is detected by package-name heuristics rather than by
         * resolving the HOME intent, so that a user-chosen third-party launcher
         * is also recognised.
         */
        fun isSystemSurface(packageName: String): Boolean {
            if (SystemOverlayPackages.isSystemSurface(packageName)) return true
            val lower = packageName.lowercase()
            if (LAUNCHER_HINTS.any { lower.contains(it) }) return true
            if (IME_HINTS.any { lower.contains(it) }) return true
            return false
        }
    }
}

FILE: app\src\main\java\com\rewardadguard\app\guard\CloseButtonGuard.kt
